claims.statement: Atum is an Egyptian primordial god from whom everything arises.
claims.statement_id: Atum adalah dewa primordial Mesir yang menjadi asal segala sesuatu.
claims.quote: is the primordial God in Egyptian mythology from whom all else arose.

claims.statement: He creates himself.
claims.statement_id: Ia menciptakan dirinya sendiri.
claims.quote: He created himself and is the father of Shu and Tefnut

claims.statement: He is the father of Shu and Tefnut.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah ayah Shu dan Tefnut.
claims.quote: He created himself and is the father of Shu and Tefnut

claims.statement: Atum is closely associated with the evening sun.
claims.statement_id: Atum erat terkait matahari senja.
claims.quote: Atum is also closely associated with the evening sun.

claims.statement: His name is connected with a verb meaning to complete or finish.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dikaitkan dengan kata kerja yang berarti melengkapi atau menyelesaikan.
claims.quote: Atum's name is thought to be derived from the verb tm which means 'to complete' or 'to finish'. Thus, he has been interpreted as being the "complete one" and also the finisher of the world, which he returns to watery chaos at the end of the creative cycle. As creator, he was seen as the progenitor of the world, the deities and universe having received his vital force or ka.

claims.statement: The Pyramid Texts combine him with Ra as Ra-Atum.
claims.statement_id: Teks Piramida memadukannya dengan Ra sebagai Ra-Atum.
claims.quote: he is sometimes syncretized with Ra to form Ra-Atum

claims.statement: Memphite theology tells of Ptah creating Atum through thought and speech.
claims.statement_id: Teologi Memphis mengisahkan Ptah menciptakan Atum melalui pikiran dan ucapan.
claims.quote: The Memphites (priests of Memphis), on the other hand, believed that Ptah created Atum in a more intellectual way, using his speech and thought, as told on the Shabaka Stone.

claims.statement: In Heliopolitan cosmogony he emerges from primordial waters on the benben mound.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kosmogoni Heliopolis ia muncul dari air primordial pada benben.
claims.quote: In the Heliopolitan Cosmogony, Atum was considered to be the first god, having created himself, sitting on a mound (benben) (or identified with the mound itself), and rose from the primordial waters (Nu). Early myths state that Atum created the god Shu and goddess Tefnut by spitting them out of his mouth.

claims.statement: He is believed to lift a king’s soul from his pyramid to the starry heavens.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya mengangkat jiwa raja dari piramida ke langit berbintang.
claims.quote: In the Old Kingdom, the Egyptians believed that Atum lifted the dead king's soul from his pyramid to the starry heavens. He was also a solar deity, associated with the primary sun god Ra. Atum was linked specifically with the evening sun, while Ra or the closely linked god Khepri were connected with the sun at morning and midday.

claims.statement: The Coffin Texts depict Atum and Osiris surviving as serpents at the universe’s end.
claims.statement_id: Teks Peti Mati menggambarkan Atum dan Osiris bertahan sebagai ular pada akhir alam semesta.
claims.quote: after millions of years he and Osiris would be the only ones to survive the end of time as serpents.

claims.statement: This source places Atum as the first god of the Ennead.
claims.statement_id: Sumber ini menempatkan Atum sebagai dewa pertama Ennead.
claims.quote: first god of the Ennead (tribunal of nine gods)

claims.statement: He uses Heka’s magical power in creation.
claims.statement_id: Ia memakai daya magis Heka dalam penciptaan.
claims.quote: draws on the magical forces of Heka to create all the other gods, human beings, and life on earth.

claims.statement: He is also described as creator of humankind.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga disebut pencipta umat manusia.
claims.quote: creator of the universe and human beings.

claims.statement: Budge distinguishes Atum as closer of the day from Ptah as opener of the day.
claims.statement_id: Budge membedakan Atum sebagai penutup hari dari Ptah sebagai pembuka hari.
claims.quote: TEMU or ATMU, i.e., the "closer" of the day, just as Ptah was the "opener" of the day.

claims.statement: Budge states that Atum’s human form was known under Fifth-Dynasty kings.
claims.statement_id: Budge menyatakan bentuk manusia Atum dikenal pada masa raja Dinasti Kelima.
claims.quote: at the time of the kings of the Vth dynasty, for his traditional form is that of a man at that time.

claims.statement: Atum was relevant to the ancient Egyptians throughout most of Egypt's history. He is believed to have been present in ideology as early as predynastic times, becoming more prevalent in the Old Kingdom and still worshiped through the Middle and New Kingdom, though overshadowed by Ra by then.
claims.statement_id: Atum penting bagi bangsa Mesir kuno hampir sepanjang sejarah Mesir. Ia dipercaya sudah hadir dalam gagasan keagamaan sejak masa pradinasti, makin menonjol pada masa Kerajaan Lama, dan terus dipuja pada masa Kerajaan Tengah dan Kerajaan Baru, walaupun saat itu ia tertutup oleh Ra.
claims.quote: Atum was relevant to the ancient Egyptians throughout most of Egypt's history. He is believed to have been present in ideology as early as predynastic times, becoming even more prevalent during the Old Kingdom and continuing to be worshiped through the Middle and New Kingdom, though he becomes overshadowed by Ra around this time.

claims.statement: According to the Heliopolitan view, Atum originally existed in his egg within the primeval waters, was born during the primordial flood, and became the source of everything created after him.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pandangan Heliopolis, Atum semula ada di dalam telurnya di perairan purba, lahir pada banjir purba, dan menjadi sumber segala sesuatu yang tercipta sesudahnya.
claims.quote: According to the Heliopolitan view, Atum originally existed in his egg within the primeval waters, being born during the primordial flood, becoming the source of everything that was created after him.

claims.statement: One text argues that Atum did not create Shu and Tefnut by spitting them out of his mouth by means of saliva and semen, but rather by Atum's lips.
claims.statement_id: Satu teks menyatakan bahwa Atum tidak menciptakan Shu dan Tefnut dengan meludahkan mereka dari mulutnya lewat air liur dan air mani, melainkan lewat bibir Atum.
claims.quote: One text debates that Atum did not create Shu and Tefnut by spitting them out of his mouth by means of saliva and semen, but rather by Atum's lips.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Shu and Tefnut were the first two gods Atum created, either by mating with his shadow or by spitting.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Shu dan Tefnut adalah dua dewa pertama yang diciptakan Atum, entah dengan bersatu dengan bayangannya atau dengan meludah.
claims.quote: Shu and Tefnut were the first two gods Atum created either by mating with his shadow or by spitting.

claims.statement: In the Coffin Texts, Atum claims that he will destroy everything he created in the beginning of existence and bring it back to Nu, the primeval waters, describing the belief that the gods and goddesses would one day cease to exist outside the primeval waters.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Teks Peti Mati, Atum menyatakan bahwa ia akan menghancurkan semua yang ia ciptakan pada awal keberadaan dan mengembalikannya ke Nu, perairan purba; ini menggambarkan kepercayaan bahwa para dewa suatu hari akan berhenti ada di luar perairan purba.
claims.quote: He claims that he will destroy everything he created in the beginning of existence and bring it back to Nu, the primeval waters, thus describing the belief that the gods and goddesses would one day cease to exist outside of the primeval waters.

claims.statement: In the Book of the Dead, which was still current in the Graeco-Roman period, the sun god Atum is said to have ascended from the chaos-waters in the appearance of a snake, the animal that renews itself every morning.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kitab Orang Mati, yang masih dipakai pada masa Yunani-Romawi, dewa matahari Atum disebut telah naik dari air kekacauan dalam rupa ular, hewan yang memperbarui dirinya setiap pagi.
claims.quote: In the Book of the Dead, which was still current in the Graeco-Roman period, the sun god Atum is said to have ascended from chaos-waters with the appearance of a snake, the animal renewing itself every morning.

claims.statement: Atum is usually depicted in human form, wearing either the divine Tripartite wig or the dual white and red crown of Upper and Lower Egypt, known as the Double Crown, reinforcing his connection with kingship.
claims.statement_id: Atum biasanya digambarkan berwujud manusia, memakai wig Tripartit ilahi atau mahkota ganda putih dan merah Mesir Hulu dan Hilir, yang dikenal sebagai Mahkota Ganda, sehingga menegaskan kaitannya dengan kerajaan.
claims.quote: Atum is usually depicted in anthropomorphic form, wearing either the divine Tripartite wig or the dual white and red crown of Upper and Lower Egypt, known as the Double Crown, reinforcing his connection with kingship.

claims.statement: Atum is sometimes also shown as a serpent, the form he returns to at the end of the creative cycle, and occasionally as a mongoose, lion, bull, lizard, or ape.
claims.statement_id: Atum kadang juga ditampilkan sebagai ular, wujud yang akan ia kembalikan pada akhir siklus penciptaan, dan sesekali sebagai luwak, singa, banteng, kadal, atau kera.
claims.quote: Sometimes he is also shown as a serpent, the form he returns to at the end of the creative cycle, and also occasionally as a mongoose, lion, bull, lizard, or ape.

claims.statement: Atum was worshiped throughout Egypt's history; the center of his worship was the city of Heliopolis (Egyptian: Annu or Iunu).
claims.statement_id: Atum dipuja sepanjang sejarah Mesir; pusat pemujaannya berada di kota Heliopolis (bahasa Mesir: Annu atau Iunu).
claims.quote: Atum was worshiped throughout Egypt's history; the center of his worship centered on the city of Heliopolis (Egyptian: Annu or Iunu).

claims.statement: The only surviving remnant of Heliopolis is the obelisk of the Temple of Ra-Atum in Al-Masalla, Al-Matariyyah, Cairo. It was erected by Senusret I of the Twelfth Dynasty and still stands in its original position.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya sisa Heliopolis yang masih ada adalah obelisk Kuil Ra-Atum di Al-Masalla, Al-Matariyyah, Kairo. Obelisk itu didirikan oleh Senusret I dari Dinasti Kedua Belas dan masih berdiri di posisi aslinya.
claims.quote: The only surviving remnant of Heliopolis is the Temple of Ra-Atum obelisk located in Al-Masalla of Al-Matariyyah, Cairo. It was erected by Senusret I of the Twelfth Dynasty, and still stands in its original position.

claims.statement: Unable to bear his loss, Atum sent a fiery messenger, the Eye of Ra, to find his children. The tears of joy he shed on their return became the first human beings.
claims.statement_id: Karena tak sanggup menanggung kehilangan, Atum mengirim utusan berapi, Mata Ra, untuk mencari anak-anaknya. Air mata gembira yang ia tumpahkan saat mereka kembali menjadi manusia pertama.
claims.quote: Unable to bear his loss, Atum sent a fiery messenger, the Eye of Ra, to find his children. The tears of joy he shed upon their return were the first human beings.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, in the story of the creation of the world Atum is angered by the intimate relationship between Geb (earth) and Nut (sky) and so separates them, declaring that Nut may not give birth to her children on any day of the year.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, dalam kisah penciptaan dunia Atum marah oleh kedekatan Geb (bumi) dan Nut (langit) sehingga memisahkan mereka dan menetapkan bahwa Nut tidak boleh melahirkan anak-anaknya pada hari mana pun dalam setahun.
claims.quote: In the story of the creation of the world, Atum is angered by the intimate relationship between Geb (earth) and Nut (sky) and so separates them, declaring that Nut may not give birth to her children on any day of the year.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Nefertum (Nefertem), the god of perfume and sweet aromas, was born from the bud of the blue lotus flower at the dawn of creation and was originally an aspect of Atum; his name means "Beautiful Atum".
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Nefertum (Nefertem), dewa wewangian dan aroma harum, lahir dari kuncup bunga teratai biru pada fajar penciptaan dan pada mulanya merupakan salah satu aspek Atum; namanya berarti "Atum yang Indah".
claims.quote: Nefertum (Nefertem) - God of perfume and sweet aromas. Nefertum was born from the bud of the blue lotus flower at the dawn of creation and was originally an aspect of Atum. His name means "Beautiful Atum".

claims.statement: Budge writes that the great god of Heliopolis was Temu or Atmu, the setting sun, and that the priests of that place ascribed to him the attributes which rightly belong to Ra, the Sun-god of the day-time.
claims.statement_id: Budge menulis bahwa dewa agung Heliopolis adalah Temu atau Atmu, matahari terbenam, dan bahwa para imam di sana menyematkan kepadanya sifat-sifat yang sebenarnya milik Ra, dewa matahari siang hari.
claims.quote: At the outset we see that the great god of Heliopolis was Temu or Atmu, the setting sun, and to him the priests of that place ascribed the attributes which rightly belong to Rā, the Sun-god of the day-time.

claims.statement: According to Budge, the priests of Heliopolis formulated the idea of a company of nine gods called the "great company (paut) of the gods", and placed the god Temu at its head.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Budge, para imam Heliopolis merumuskan gagasan kelompok sembilan dewa yang disebut "kelompok agung (paut) para dewa", dan di kepala kelompok itu mereka menempatkan dewa Temu.
claims.quote: For some reason or other they formulated the idea of a company of the gods, nine in number, which was called the "great company (paut) of the gods," and at the head of this company they placed the god Temu.

claims.statement: Budge writes that the setting sun, called Temu or Atmu, the rising sun, called Khepera, and the mid-day sun, called Ra, were three forms of the same god.
claims.statement_id: Budge menulis bahwa matahari terbenam yang disebut Temu atau Atmu, matahari terbit yang disebut Khepera, dan matahari tengah hari yang disebut Ra adalah tiga wujud dari dewa yang sama.
claims.quote: Thus the setting sun, called Temu or Atmu, and the rising sun, called Khepera, and the mid-day sun, called Rā, were three forms of the same god

claims.statement: In the Book of the Dead chapter of opening the mouth, the speaker asks that Thoth loose the bandages of Set which fetter his mouth and that the god Tem hurl them at those who would fetter him with them and drive them back.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pasal Kitab Orang Mati tentang pembukaan mulut, sang penutur memohon agar Thoth melepaskan perban Set yang membelenggu mulutnya dan agar dewa Tem melemparkannya kepada mereka yang hendak membelenggunya dengan perban itu, lalu menghalau mereka.
claims.quote: Moreover, may Thoth, being filled and furnished with charms, come and loose the bandages, even the bandages of Set which fetter my mouth; and may the god Tem hurl them at those who would fetter [me] with them, and drive them back.

claims.statement: In the text translated by Budge, the word of power of Tem, the Father of the gods, who is in heaven, maketh to live.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks terjemahan Budge, kata kuasa Tem, Bapa para dewa, yang ada di surga, memberi hidup.
claims.quote: The word of power of Tem, the Father of the gods, who is in heaven, maketh to live.

claims.statement: Atum is the god of pre-existence and post-existence.
claims.statement_id: Atum adalah dewa pra-keberadaan dan pasca-keberadaan.
claims.quote: Atum is the god of pre-existence and post-existence.

claims.statement: Khepri-Atum encompassed sunrise and sunset, thus reflecting the entire cycle of morning and evening.
claims.statement_id: Khepri-Atum mencakup matahari terbit dan matahari terbenam, sehingga mencerminkan seluruh siklus pagi dan petang.
claims.quote: Khepri-Atum encompassed sunrise and sunset, thus reflecting the entire cycle of morning and evening.

claims.statement: Mut is a mother goddess worshipped in ancient Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Mut adalah dewi ibu yang dipuja di Mesir kuno.
claims.quote: was a mother goddess worshipped in ancient Egypt.

claims.statement: Her name means mother.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti ibu.
claims.quote: Her name means mother in the ancient Egyptian language.

claims.statement: She is connected with Nu’s primordial waters.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkaitan dengan air primordial Nu.
claims.quote: Mut was considered a primal deity, associated with the primordial waters of Nu from which everything in the world was born.

claims.statement: Some accounts describe her giving birth to the world without a partner.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kisah menyebutnya melahirkan dunia tanpa pasangan.
claims.quote: Mut was sometimes said to have given birth to the world through parthenogenesis

claims.statement: Amun-Ra is more often named as her husband.
claims.statement_id: Amun-Ra lebih sering disebut sebagai suaminya.
claims.quote: more often she was said to have a husband, the solar creator god Amun-Ra.

claims.statement: Khonsu is the lunar child associated with her.
claims.statement_id: Khonsu adalah anak bulan yang terkait dengannya.
claims.quote: she was particularly associated as the mother of the lunar child god Khonsu.

claims.statement: Mut, Amun-Ra and Khonsu form the Theban triad at Karnak.
claims.statement_id: Mut, Amun-Ra, dan Khonsu membentuk triad Thebes di Karnak.
claims.quote: the family of Amun-Ra, Mut and Khonsu were worshipped together as the Theban Triad.

claims.statement: Art depicts her wearing Egypt’s double crown.
claims.statement_id: Seni menggambarkannya memakai mahkota ganda Mesir.
claims.quote: In art, Mut was usually depicted as a woman wearing the double crown of the kings of Egypt, representing her power over the whole of the land.

claims.statement: Rulers supported her worship to assert their authority.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaannya didukung penguasa untuk menegaskan kewenangan mereka.
claims.quote: During the high point of Mut's cult, the rulers of Egypt would support her worship in their own way to emphasize their own authority and right to rule through an association with Mut. Mut was involved in many ancient Egyptian festivals such as the Opet Festival and the Beautiful Festival of the Valley.

claims.statement: She participates in the Opet Festival and Beautiful Festival of the Valley.
claims.statement_id: Ia terlibat dalam Festival Opet dan Festival Lembah.
claims.quote: Mut was involved in many ancient Egyptian festivals such as the Opet Festival and the Beautiful Festival of the Valley.

claims.statement: Spell 164 of the Book of the Dead portrays Mut saving souls from demons.
claims.statement_id: Mantra 164 Kitab Orang Mati menggambarkan Mut menyelamatkan jiwa dari setan.
claims.quote: in Spell 164 of the Book of the Dead, is depicted as a savior of souls trapped by demons in the afterlife.

claims.statement: She is a divine protector of the king and state.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah pelindung ilahi raja dan negara.
claims.quote: She was also the divine protector of the king and state

claims.statement: This source describes her burning traitors in a flaming brazier.
claims.statement_id: Sumber ini menyebutnya membakar pengkhianat dalam anglo api.
claims.quote: roasted conspirators and traitors in her flaming brazier.

claims.statement: She is linked with Bastet and Sekhmet as a protective goddess.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan Bastet dan Sekhmet sebagai dewi pelindung.
claims.quote: Mut was a protector deity associated with Bastet and Sekhmet.

claims.statement: Mackenzie records Mut’s forms as a vulture and a lioness.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mencatat bentuk Mut sebagai burung nasar dan singa betina.
claims.quote: She is represented as a vulture and also as a lioness.

claims.statement: Sekhmet is an Egyptian warrior and healing goddess.
claims.statement_id: Sekhmet adalah dewi prajurit dan penyembuhan dalam mitologi Mesir.
claims.quote: is a warrior goddess as well as goddess of medicine.

claims.statement: Sekhmet is also a solar deity with the epithet Eye of Ra.
claims.statement_id: Sekhmet juga merupakan dewi matahari dengan gelar Mata Ra.
claims.quote: Sekhmet is also a solar deity, sometimes given the epithet "the eye of Ra".

claims.statement: She is often associated with Hathor and Bastet.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering dikaitkan dengan Hathor dan Bastet.
claims.quote: She is often associated with the goddesses Hathor and Bastet.

claims.statement: Sekhmet is a vengeful manifestation of Ra called the Eye of Ra.
claims.statement_id: Sekhmet adalah manifestasi pembalasan Ra yang disebut Mata Ra.
claims.quote: Sekhmet acted as the vengeful manifestation of Ra's power, the Eye of Ra.

claims.statement: She is believed to cause plagues and is also invoked for healing.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap menyebabkan wabah, sekaligus dimohon untuk menyembuhkan.
claims.quote: She is also believed to cause plagues ... she is also called upon to ward off disease and heal the sick.

claims.statement: Ra sends Hathor as Sekhmet to punish conspiring mortals.
claims.statement_id: Ra mengirim Hathor dalam bentuk Sekhmet menghukum manusia yang bersekongkol.
claims.quote: Ra sends the goddess Hathor, in the form of Sekhmet, to destroy mortals who conspired against him.

claims.statement: The gods stop her with red beer mistaken for blood.
claims.statement_id: Para dewa menghentikannya dengan bir merah yang disangka darah.
claims.quote: They poured out a lake of beer dyed with red ochre so that it resembled blood. Mistaking the beer for blood, Sekhmet drank it all and became so drunk that she gave up on the slaughter and returned peacefully to Ra.

claims.statement: Another version tells of Thoth persuading Sekhmet to return after she leaves Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain mengisahkan Thoth membujuk Sekhmet kembali setelah ia meninggalkan Mesir.
claims.quote: In other versions of this story, Sekhmet grew angered at the deception and left Egypt, diminishing the power of the sun. This threatened the power and security of the world; thus, she was persuaded by the god Thoth to return and restore the sun to its full glory.

claims.statement: She is Ptah’s wife and Nefertum’s mother.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah istri Ptah dan ibu Nefertum.
claims.quote: Sekhmet was considered the wife of the god Ptah and mother of his son Nefertum.

claims.statement: A festival of intoxication reenacts the drinking that calms her mythical wrath.
claims.statement_id: Festival mabuk mengulang minum yang meredakan amarahnya dalam mitos.
claims.quote: During an annual festival held at the beginning of the year, a festival of intoxication, the Egyptians danced and played music to soothe the wildness of the goddess and drank great quantities of beer and wine ritually to imitate the extreme drunkenness that stopped the wrath of the goddess—when she almost destroyed humanity.

claims.statement: Her name is interpreted as the Powerful One.
claims.statement_id: Namanya diartikan Yang Perkasa.
claims.quote: Her name means "Powerful" and is usually interpreted as "The Female Powerful One".

claims.statement: She becomes a military patron through destruction and vengeance.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi pelindung militer melalui kekuatan penghancuran dan pembalasan.
claims.quote: was the patron deity of the military for her powers of destruction and vengeance.

claims.statement: One of her titles is Smiter of the Nubians.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu gelarnya adalah Penghantam Orang Nubia.
claims.quote: She was known as "Smiter of the Nubians" in this regard but she also brought natural disaster.

claims.statement: The Mistress of Life title relates to her ability to cure plague.
claims.statement_id: Gelar Nyonya Kehidupan berkaitan dengan kemampuannya menyembuhkan wabah.
claims.quote: she could cure it and was known as "Mistress of Life" in this capacity

claims.statement: Budge uses Sekhet for Ptah’s feminine counterpart in a triad with Nefertem.
claims.statement_id: Budge memakai nama Sekhet untuk pasangan feminin Ptah dalam triad bersama Nefertem.
claims.quote: His feminine counterpart was the goddess SEKHET, and the third member of the triad of which he was the chief was NEFER-TEMU.
claims.detail: tidak bisa dibuka (fetch failed); dicek lewat arsip Wayback

claims.statement: Geb is the Egyptian earth god and a member of the Heliopolitan Ennead.
claims.statement_id: Geb adalah dewa bumi Mesir dan anggota Ennead Heliopolis.
claims.quote: was the Egyptian god of the Earth and a mythological member of the Ennead of Heliopolis.

claims.statement: His laughter is believed to produce earthquakes.
claims.statement_id: Tawanya dipercaya menghasilkan gempa bumi.
claims.quote: It was believed in ancient Egypt that Geb's laughter generated earthquakes and that he allowed crops to grow.

claims.statement: He also enables crops to grow.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga memungkinkan tanaman tumbuh.
claims.quote: It was believed in ancient Egypt that Geb's laughter generated earthquakes and that he allowed crops to grow.

claims.statement: The earliest representation cited by the article dates to Djoser’s reign.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran tertua yang disebut artikel berasal dari masa Djoser.
claims.quote: The oldest representation in a fragmentary relief of the god was as an anthropomorphic bearded being accompanied by his name, and dating from king Djoser's reign, during the Third Dynasty, and was found in Heliopolis. However, the god never received a temple of his own.

claims.statement: He is sometimes depicted as a ram, bull or crocodile.
claims.statement_id: Ia kadang digambarkan sebagai domba, banteng, atau buaya.
claims.quote: In later times he could also be depicted as a ram, a bull or a crocodile

claims.statement: Budge recounts Geb and Nut uniting every evening until Shu separates them in the morning.
claims.statement_id: Budge mengisahkan Geb dan Nut bersatu setiap malam, lalu Shu memisahkan mereka pada pagi hari.
claims.quote: These deities were supposed to unite every evening, and to remain embraced until the morning, when the god Shu separated them

claims.statement: Nut is his wife and Shu and Tefnut are his parents.
claims.statement_id: Nut adalah istrinya, sedangkan Shu dan Tefnut adalah orang tuanya.
claims.quote: In the Heliopolitan Ennead (a group of nine gods created in the beginning by the one god Atum or Ra), Geb is the husband of Nut, the sky or visible daytime and nightly firmament, the son of the earlier primordial elements Tefnut (moisture) and Shu ("emptiness"), and the father to the four lesser gods of the system – Osiris, Seth, Isis and Nephthys.

claims.statement: His children include Osiris, Set, Isis and Nephthys.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anaknya mencakup Osiris, Set, Isis, dan Nephthys.
claims.quote: the father to the four lesser gods of the system – Osiris, Seth, Isis and Nephthys.

claims.statement: Shu separates Geb from Nut.
claims.statement_id: Shu memisahkan Geb dari Nut.
claims.quote: Geb was believed to have originally been engaged with Nut and had to be separated from her by Shu, god of the air.

claims.statement: His representations may show plants on his body.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya dapat memuat tanaman pada tubuhnya.
claims.quote: was depicted with plants and other green patches on his body.

claims.statement: World History Encyclopedia identifies Geb with earth and growing plants.
claims.statement_id: World History Encyclopedia menegaskan Geb sebagai dewa bumi dan tumbuhan yang tumbuh.
claims.quote: Geb - God of the earth and growing things.

claims.statement: Budge records the title hereditary chief of the gods for Geb.
claims.statement_id: Budge mencatat gelar kepala turun-temurun para dewa bagi Geb.
claims.quote: He is called the "Erpā," i.e., the "hereditary chief" of the gods

claims.statement: According to Budge, Geb’s role develops into a god of the dead because they are buried in the earth.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Budge, peran Geb berkembang menjadi dewa orang mati karena mereka dimakamkan di bumi.
claims.quote: later he became a god of the dead as representing the earth wherein the deceased was laid.

claims.statement: Budge connects Geb and Nut with providing food for the dead.
claims.statement_id: Budge menghubungkan Geb dan Nut dengan pemberian makanan bagi orang mati.
claims.quote: she and her husband Seb were considered to be the givers of food, not only to the living but also to the dead.

claims.statement: Budge also records the title father of the gods for Geb.
claims.statement_id: Budge juga mencatat gelar ayah para dewa untuk Geb.
claims.quote: the "father of the gods," these being, of course, Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys.

claims.statement: Geb could also be considered a father of snakes.
claims.statement_id: Geb juga dapat dianggap sebagai ayah ular-ular.
claims.quote: He could also be considered a father of snakes.

claims.statement: Geb also often occurs as a primeval divine king of Egypt from whom his son Osiris and his grandson Horus inherited the land after many conflicts with the disruptive god Set, brother and killer of Osiris.
claims.statement_id: Geb juga sering muncul sebagai raja ilahi purba Mesir; putranya Osiris dan cucunya Horus mewarisi negeri itu darinya setelah banyak pertikaian dengan dewa pengacau Set, saudara dan pembunuh Osiris.
claims.quote: Geb also often occurs as a primeval divine king of Egypt from whom his son Osiris and his grandson Horus inherited the land after many conflicts with the disruptive god Set, brother and killer of Osiris.

claims.statement: Geb could also be regarded as personified fertile earth and barren desert, the latter containing the dead or setting them free from their tombs, metaphorically described as "Geb opening his jaws".
claims.statement_id: Geb juga dapat dipandang sebagai perwujudan tanah subur dan gurun tandus; gurun itu menampung orang mati atau membebaskan mereka dari makamnya, yang secara kiasan disebut "Geb membuka rahangnya".
claims.quote: Geb could also be regarded as personified fertile earth and barren desert, the latter containing the dead or setting them free from their tombs, metaphorically described as "Geb opening his jaws"

claims.statement: Geb and Nut together formed the permanent boundary between the primeval waters and the newly created world.
claims.statement_id: Geb dan Nut bersama-sama membentuk batas tetap antara perairan purba dan dunia yang baru tercipta.
claims.quote: Geb and Nut together formed the permanent boundary between the primeval waters and the newly created world.

claims.statement: As a chthonic deity Geb became naturally associated with the underworld, fresh waters and vegetation; barley is said to grow upon his ribs.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa bawah tanah (chthonic), Geb secara alami dikaitkan dengan dunia bawah, air tawar, dan tumbuh-tumbuhan; jelai dikatakan tumbuh di rusuknya.
claims.quote: As a chthonic deity he (like Min) became naturally associated with the underworld, fresh waters and with vegetation – barley being said to grow upon his ribs

claims.statement: In Greco-Roman Egypt, Geb was equated with the Greek titan Cronus, because Cronus held a quite similar position in the Greek pantheon, as the father of the gods Zeus, Hades and Poseidon, as Geb did in Egyptian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Di Mesir masa Yunani-Romawi, Geb disamakan dengan Titan Yunani Cronus karena Cronus memegang kedudukan yang cukup mirip dalam panteon Yunani, sebagai ayah para dewa Zeus, Hades, dan Poseidon, sebagaimana Geb dalam mitologi Mesir.
claims.quote: In Greco-Roman Egypt, Geb was equated with the Greek titan Cronus, because he held a quite similar position in the Greek pantheon, as the father of the gods Zeus, Hades, and Poseidon, as Geb did in Egyptian mythology.

claims.statement: This equation of Geb with Cronus is particularly well attested in Tebtunis in the southern Fayyum, where the two were part of a local version of the cult of Sobek, the crocodile god.
claims.statement_id: Persamaan Geb dengan Cronus ini terutama terbukti di Tebtunis, Fayum selatan: di sana keduanya menjadi bagian dari versi lokal pemujaan Sobek, dewa buaya.
claims.quote: This equation is particularly well attested in Tebtunis in the southern Fayyum: Geb and Cronus were here part of a local version of the cult of Sobek, the crocodile god.

claims.statement: In the Book of the Heavenly Cow, it is implied that Geb is the heir of the departing sun god. After Geb passed the throne to his son Osiris, he took on the role of a judge in the Divine Tribunal of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kitab Sapi Surgawi, tersirat bahwa Geb adalah pewaris dewa matahari yang pergi. Setelah menyerahkan takhta kepada putranya Osiris, Geb berperan sebagai hakim dalam Pengadilan Ilahi para dewa.
claims.quote: In the Book of the Heavenly Cow, it is implied that Geb is the heir of the departing sun god. After Geb passed on the throne to Osiris, his son, he then took on a role of a judge in the Divine Tribunal of the gods.

claims.statement: Some Egyptologists have stated that Geb was associated with a mythological divine creator goose, who had laid a world egg from which the sun and/or the world had sprung.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa Egiptolog menyatakan bahwa Geb dikaitkan dengan angsa pencipta ilahi mitologis yang telah bertelur sebuah telur dunia, tempat matahari dan/atau dunia berasal.
claims.quote: Some Egyptologists (specifically Jan Bergman, Terence Duquesne and Richard H. Wilkinson) have stated that Geb was associated with a mythological divine creator goose, who had laid a world egg from which the sun and/or the world had sprung.

claims.statement: This theory is assumed to be incorrect and to result from confusing the divine name "Geb" with that of a Whitefronted Goose.
claims.statement_id: Teori itu diasumsikan keliru dan merupakan hasil dari keliru menyamakan nama ilahi "Geb" dengan nama angsa dahi putih.
claims.quote: This theory is assumed to be incorrect and to be a result of confusing the divine name "Geb" with that of a Whitefronted Goose

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, after the primordial mound rose from the waters of chaos Atum (Ra) sent his children Shu and Tefnut out to create the world; when they returned, his tears of joy became human beings. These creatures had nowhere to live, so Shu and Tefnut mated to give birth to Geb (earth) and Nut (sky).
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, setelah gundukan purba muncul dari air kekacauan, Atum (Ra) mengutus anak-anaknya Shu dan Tefnut menciptakan dunia; ketika mereka kembali, air mata gembira Atum menjadi manusia. Manusia itu tidak punya tempat tinggal, maka Shu dan Tefnut kawin dan melahirkan Geb (bumi) dan Nut (langit).
claims.quote: After the primordial mound rose from the waters of chaos at creation, Atum (Ra) sent his children Shu and Tefnut out to create the world. When they returned, he was so happy he shed tears of joy which became human beings. These creatures had nowhere to live and so Shu and Tefnut mated to give birth to Geb (earth) and Nut (sky).

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, in the story of the creation of the world Atum is angered by the intimate relationship between Geb (earth) and Nut (sky) and so separates them, declaring that Nut may not give birth to her children on any day of the year.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, dalam kisah penciptaan dunia Atum marah oleh kedekatan Geb (bumi) dan Nut (langit) sehingga memisahkan mereka dan menetapkan bahwa Nut tidak boleh melahirkan anak-anaknya pada hari mana pun dalam setahun.
claims.quote: In the story of the creation of the world, Atum is angered by the intimate relationship between Geb (earth) and Nut (sky) and so separates them, declaring that Nut may not give birth to her children on any day of the year.

claims.statement: Budge writes that, according to an old view, Seb and Nut existed in the primeval watery abyss side by side with Shu and Tefnut, and later Seb became the earth and Nut the sky.
claims.statement_id: Budge menulis bahwa menurut pandangan lama, Seb dan Nut berada di jurang perairan purba berdampingan dengan Shu dan Tefnut, dan kemudian Seb menjadi bumi serta Nut menjadi langit.
claims.quote: According to an old view, Seb and Nut existed in the primeval watery abyss side by side with Shu and Tefnut; and later Seb became the earth and Nut the sky.

claims.statement: In a hymn to Ra quoted by Budge, Ra, who brings forth green things in their season, is told that his body is Seb.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah himne untuk Ra yang dikutip Budge, Ra, yang menumbuhkan tanaman hijau pada musimnya, disapa dengan kata bahwa tubuhnya adalah Seb.
claims.quote: Praise be unto thee, O Rā, thou exalted Power, who bringest forth, green things in their season, behold [thy] body is Seb.

claims.statement: In the Book of the Dead chapter on transformation into Ptah, the speaker declares that he is decreed to be the divine heir of Seb, the lord of the earth, and to be the protector therein.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pasal Kitab Orang Mati tentang perubahan wujud menjadi Ptah, sang penutur menyatakan bahwa ia ditetapkan sebagai pewaris ilahi Seb, penguasa bumi, dan pelindung di dalamnya.
claims.quote: I am decreed to be the divine Heir of Seb, the lord of the earth and to be the protector therein.

claims.statement: In the text translated by Budge, when Seb had come, the god who is speaking said to him, "Let war be made against thy worms (or, serpents) which are in thee".
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks terjemahan Budge, ketika Seb datang, sang dewa yang berbicara berkata kepadanya, "Biarlah perang dilancarkan terhadap cacing-cacingmu (atau ular-ularmu) yang ada di dalam dirimu".
claims.quote: And when the Majesty of Seb had come, the Majesty of this god said unto him, "Let war be made against thy worms (or, serpents) which are in thee

claims.statement: Shu is a primordial air god in Egyptian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Shu adalah dewa udara primordial dalam mitologi Mesir.
claims.quote: Shu - The primordial god of the air whose name means "Emptiness".

claims.statement: Tefnut is his sister and wife.
claims.statement_id: Tefnut adalah saudari sekaligus istrinya.
claims.quote: spouse and brother to the goddess Tefnut

claims.statement: Atum creates Shu and Tefnut in the Heliopolitan account.
claims.statement_id: Atum menciptakan Shu dan Tefnut dalam kisah Heliopolis.
claims.quote: In Heliopolitan theology, Atum created the first couple of the Ennead, Shu and Tefnut, by masturbating or by spitting. Shu was the father of Nut and Geb and grandfather of Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys. His great-grandsons are Horus and Anubis.

claims.statement: Shu is the father of Nut and Geb.
claims.statement_id: Shu adalah ayah Nut dan Geb.
claims.quote: Shu was the father of Nut and Geb

claims.statement: The air he represents is considered cooling and calming.
claims.statement_id: Udara yang diwakilinya dianggap menyejukkan dan menenangkan.
claims.quote: As the air, Shu was considered to be a cooling, and thus a calming influence and pacifier. Due to the association with dry air, calm, and thus Ma'at (truth, justice, order, and balance), Shu was depicted as the dry air/atmosphere between the Earth and sky, separating the two realms after the event of the First Occasion. Shu was also portrayed in art as wearing an ostrich feather.

claims.statement: He is shown wearing an ostrich feather signifying lightness and emptiness.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan memakai bulu burung unta sebagai lambang ringan dan kosong.
claims.quote: Shu was also portrayed in art as wearing an ostrich feather. ... The ostrich feather was symbolic of lightness and emptiness.

claims.statement: Mist and clouds are also associated with Shu.
claims.statement_id: Kabut dan awan juga dikaitkan dengan Shu.
claims.quote: Fog and clouds were also Shu's elements and they were often called his bones.

claims.statement: One myth tells of Tefnut leaving Egypt after a quarrel with Shu.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah mitos mengisahkan Tefnut meninggalkan Mesir setelah bertengkar dengan Shu.
claims.quote: In a much later myth, representing a terrible weather disaster at the end of the Old Kingdom, it's said that Tefnut and Shu once argued, and Tefnut left Egypt for Nubia (which was always more temperate). It was said that Shu quickly decided that he missed her, but she changed into a cat that destroyed any man or god that approached.

claims.statement: The Greeks associate him with Atlas who supports the heavens.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yunani menghubungkannya dengan Atlas yang menopang langit.
claims.quote: The Greeks associated Shu with Atlas, the primordial Titan who held up the celestial spheres, as they are both depicted holding up the sky.

claims.statement: He is usually human, sometimes lion-headed when defending the sun god.
claims.statement_id: Ia umumnya berupa manusia, kadang berkepala singa saat membela dewa matahari.
claims.quote: Shu is mostly represented as a human. Only in his function as a fighter and defender of the sun god is he sometimes depicted with a lion's head. He carries an ankh, the symbol of life.

claims.statement: Shu’s name is translated as Emptiness.
claims.statement_id: Nama Shu diterjemahkan sebagai Kekosongan.
claims.quote: The primordial god of the air whose name means "Emptiness".

claims.statement: One tale has the Eye of Ra search for Shu and Tefnut after a long absence.
claims.statement_id: Satu kisah mengisahkan Mata Ra mencari Shu dan Tefnut yang lama pergi.
claims.quote: The two were gone so long that Atum came to miss them and sent his eye (the Eye of Ra) in search of them.

claims.statement: Their return makes Atum weep for joy and his tears become humans.
claims.statement_id: Kepulangan mereka membuat Atum menangis bahagia dan air matanya menjadi manusia.
claims.quote: When the eye returned with them, Atum was so happy he cried and his tears created human beings.

claims.statement: Mist is called Lakes of Shu in this source.
claims.statement_id: Kabut disebut Danau Shu dalam uraian sumber ini.
claims.quote: Mist was attributed to him as "Lakes of Shu" and the clouds as "Bones of Shu"

claims.statement: Budge describes four pillars at the cardinal points as Shu’s sky supports.
claims.statement_id: Budge menjelaskan empat pilar di arah mata angin sebagai penopang langit Shu.
claims.quote: To assist him in this work he placed a pillar at each of the cardinal points, and the "supports of Shu" are thus the props of the sky.
claims.detail: tidak bisa dibuka (fetch failed); dicek lewat arsip Wayback

claims.statement: Apophis or Apep is an Egyptian chaos deity usually taking the form of a great serpent.
claims.statement_id: Apophis atau Apep adalah dewa kekacauan Mesir yang biasanya berwujud ular besar.
claims.quote: is the ancient Egyptian deity of chaos, darkness and fire ... usually depicted as a giant snake or serpent.

claims.statement: He becomes Ra’s greatest enemy.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi musuh utama Ra.
claims.quote: Because Ra was the solar deity, bringer of light, and thus the upholder of Maat, Apophis was viewed as the greatest enemy of Ra, and thus was given the title Enemy of Ra, and also "the Lord of Chaos".

claims.statement: He bears the titles Enemy of Ra and Lord of Chaos.
claims.statement_id: Ia mendapat gelar Musuh Ra dan Penguasa Kekacauan.
claims.quote: the title Enemy of Ra, and also "the Lord of Chaos".

claims.statement: Some accounts give him a head of flint.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa uraian memberikan kepala dari batu api.
claims.quote: Some descriptions said that he stretched 16 yards in length and had a head made of flint.

claims.statement: His origins vary across myths, including Ra’s umbilical cord or Nu’s primordial waters.
claims.statement_id: Asalnya berbeda antar mitos, termasuk dari pusar Ra atau air primordial Nu.
claims.quote: usually from his umbilical cord. ... existed from the beginning of time in the waters of Nu of primeval chaos.

claims.statement: Accounts of his battles with Ra expand during the New Kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Kisah pertempurannya dengan Ra diperluas pada Kerajaan Baru.
claims.quote: Tales of Apophis battles against Ra were elaborated during the New Kingdom. Storytellers said that every day Apophis must lie below the horizon and not persist in the mortal kingdom. This appropriately made him a part of the underworld.

claims.statement: Some tales place him at western Mount Manu, others just before dawn.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kisah menempatkannya di gunung barat Manu, lainnya menjelang fajar.
claims.quote: In some stories, Apophis waited for Ra in a western mountain called Manu, where the sun set, and in others, Apophis lurked just before dawn, in the Tenth region of the Night.

claims.statement: His magical gaze is believed to overwhelm Ra and his entourage.
claims.statement_id: Tatapan sihirnya dipercaya dapat melemahkan Ra dan rombongannya.
claims.quote: The Coffin Texts imply that Apophis used a magical gaze to overwhelm Ra and his entourage. Ra was assisted by a number of defenders who travelled with him, including Set and possibly the Eye of Ra. Apophis' movements were thought to cause earthquakes, and his battles with Set may have been meant to explain the origin of thunderstorms.

claims.statement: Set is among Ra’s defenders in that struggle.
claims.statement_id: Set termasuk pembela Ra dalam pertarungan itu.
claims.quote: Ra was assisted by a number of defenders who travelled with him, including Set and possibly the Eye of Ra.

claims.statement: Priestly prayers and rituals aim to ensure Ra’s victory each night.
claims.statement_id: Doa dan ritual pendeta bertujuan menjamin kemenangan Ra setiap malam.
claims.quote: Ra's victory each night was thought to be ensured by the prayers of the Egyptian priests and worshippers at temples. The Egyptians practiced a number of rituals and superstitions that were thought to ward off Apophis and to aid Ra in continuing his journey across the sky.

claims.statement: The justified dead help Ra confront Apep.
claims.statement_id: Orang mati yang dibenarkan membantu Ra menghadapi Apep.
claims.quote: Gods and the justified dead would help Ra fend the serprent off.

claims.statement: The temple ritual Overthrowing of Apophis aims to protect the solar barque.
claims.statement_id: Ritual kuil bernama Overthrowing of Apophis bertujuan menjaga bahtera matahari.
claims.quote: The ritual known as Overthrowing of Apophis was performed in temples to help the gods and departed souls protect the barge and ensure the coming of day.

claims.statement: In Budge’s account, Ra attacks Apep with fiery darts.
claims.statement_id: Dalam uraian Budge, Ra menyerang Apep dengan anak panah api.
claims.quote: the fiery darts which he discharged into the body of =Apep scorched and burnt him up

claims.statement: Apep’s attendants are also destroyed by fire.
claims.statement_id: Pengikut Apep juga dibinasakan oleh api.
claims.quote: the fiends that were in attendance upon this terrible foe were also destroyed by fire

claims.statement: Budge reads that struggle as an image of the daily conflict between light and darkness.
claims.statement_id: Budge membaca pertarungan itu sebagai gambaran perselisihan harian terang dan gelap.
claims.quote: it represented originally the fight which was supposed to go on daily between light and darkness.

claims.statement: As the solar barge sailed through the darkness, Apophis attacked it, seeking to kill Ra and prevent sunrise.
claims.statement_id: Saat bahtera matahari berlayar menembus kegelapan, Apophis menyerangnya dengan tujuan membunuh Ra dan mencegah matahari terbit.
claims.quote: As it sailed through the darkness, it was attacked by Apophis who sought to kill Ra and prevent sunrise.

claims.statement: Apophis became the sun god's enemy because the sun was the first sign of the created world and symbolized divine order, light and life; if he could swallow the sun god, he could return the world to a unity of darkness.
claims.statement_id: Apophis menjadi musuh dewa matahari karena matahari adalah tanda pertama dunia yang tercipta dan melambangkan tatanan ilahi, terang, dan kehidupan; jika ia dapat menelan dewa matahari, ia dapat mengembalikan dunia pada kesatuan kegelapan.
claims.quote: Apophis became the enemy of the sun god because the sun was the first sign of the created world and symbolized divine order, light, life, and if he could swallow the sun god, he could return the world to a unity of darkness.

claims.statement: Apophis is associated with earthquakes, thunder, darkness, storms and death, and is sometimes linked to the god Set.
claims.statement_id: Apophis dikaitkan dengan gempa bumi, guntur, kegelapan, badai, dan kematian, dan kadang dihubungkan dengan dewa Set.
claims.quote: Apophis is associated with earthquakes, thunder, darkness, storms, and death, and is sometimes linked to the god Set

claims.statement: However many times Apophis was defeated and killed, he always rose again and attacked the sun god's boat; the most powerful gods and goddesses defeated the serpent in the course of every night.
claims.statement_id: Betapapun sering Apophis dikalahkan dan dibunuh, ia selalu hidup kembali dan menyerang perahu dewa matahari; dewa dan dewi paling perkasa mengalahkan ular itu sepanjang setiap malam.
claims.quote: No matter how many times Apophis was defeated and killed, he always rose again to life and attacked the sun god's boat. The most powerful gods and goddesses would defeat the serpent in the course of every night

claims.statement: In the Book of Gates, goddesses capture Apophis and restrain him in nets held down by monkeys, the sons of Horus and the earth god Geb, and he is chopped into pieces; the next night the serpent is whole again.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kitab Gerbang, para dewi menangkap Apophis dan menahannya dalam jaring yang ditindih monyet, putra-putra Horus, dan dewa bumi Geb, lalu ia dipotong-potong; malam berikutnya ular itu utuh kembali.
claims.quote: capture Apophis and restrain him in nets held down by monkeys, the sons of Horus, and the great earth god Geb, where he is then chopped into pieces; the next night, though, the serpent is whole again

claims.statement: Cloudy days or storms were signs that Apophis was gaining ground, and solar eclipses were times of terror for the Egyptians, interpreted as a sign of Ra's demise.
claims.statement_id: Hari berawan atau badai dianggap tanda Apophis menang angin, dan gerhana matahari menjadi saat teror bagi orang Mesir karena ditafsirkan sebagai tanda kematian Ra.
claims.quote: Cloudy days or storms were signs that Apophis was gaining ground, and solar eclipses were particular times of terror for the Egyptians, as they were interpreted as a sign of Ra's demise.

claims.statement: According to the article, Apophis represented everything the Egyptians feared: darkness, oblivion and the loss of one's identity.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, Apophis mewakili segala yang ditakuti orang Mesir: kegelapan, kelupaan, dan hilangnya jati diri.
claims.quote: Apophis, then, represented everything the Egyptians feared: darkness, oblivion, and the loss of one's identity.

claims.statement: His terrifying roar was thought to make the underworld rumble.
claims.statement_id: Auman Apophis yang mengerikan dipercaya membuat dunia bawah bergemuruh.
claims.quote: It was thought that his terrifying roar would cause the underworld to rumble.

claims.statement: Priests would build an effigy of Apophis thought to contain all the evil and darkness in Egypt and burn it to protect everyone from Apophis' evil for another year.
claims.statement_id: Para pendeta membuat patung Apophis yang dipercaya memuat seluruh kejahatan dan kegelapan di Mesir, lalu membakarnya untuk melindungi semua orang dari kejahatan Apophis selama setahun lagi.
claims.quote: priests would build an effigy of Apophis that was thought to contain all of the evil and darkness in Egypt, and burn it to protect everyone from Apophis' evil for another year.

claims.statement: Because Apophis was thought to live in the underworld, he was sometimes called an Eater of Souls, so the dead also needed protection and were sometimes buried with spells that could destroy Apophis.
claims.statement_id: Karena Apophis dianggap hidup di dunia bawah, ia kadang disebut Pemakan Jiwa, sehingga orang mati juga perlu perlindungan dan kadang dikuburkan bersama mantra yang dapat membinasakan Apophis.
claims.quote: As Apophis was thought to live in the underworld, he was sometimes thought of as an Eater of Souls. Thus the dead also needed protection, so they were sometimes buried with spells that could destroy Apophis

claims.statement: Khonsu is an ancient Egyptian moon god.
claims.statement_id: Khonsu adalah dewa bulan Mesir kuno.
claims.quote: is an ancient Egyptian god of the Moon.

claims.statement: His name means traveller and is connected with the moon’s journey.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti pengelana, dihubungkan dengan perjalanan bulan.
claims.quote: His name means 'traveller', and this may relate to the perceived nightly travel of the Moon across the sky.

claims.statement: He forms the Theban triad with his mother Mut and father Amun.
claims.statement_id: Ia membentuk triad Thebes bersama ibu Mut dan ayah Amun.
claims.quote: At Thebes, he formed part of a family triad (the "Theban Triad") with Mut his mother and Amun his father.

claims.statement: Art often depicts him as a mummy with a child’s sidelock.
claims.statement_id: Seni sering menggambarkannya sebagai mumi dengan rambut samping anak-anak.
claims.quote: In art, Khonsu is typically depicted as a mummy with the symbol of childhood, a sidelock of hair, as well as the menat necklace with crook and flail. He has close links to other divine children such as Horus and Shu. He was also portrayed with the head of a falcon and like Horus, with whom he is associated as a protector and healer, adorned with the moon disk and crescent moon.

claims.statement: He may also be falcon-headed with the lunar disk and crescent.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dapat berkepala elang dengan cakram dan sabit bulan.
claims.quote: He was also portrayed with the head of a falcon ... adorned with the moon disk and crescent moon.

claims.statement: He is mentioned in the Pyramid Texts and Coffin Texts.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut dalam Teks Piramida dan Teks Peti Mati.
claims.quote: Khonsu is mentioned in the Pyramid Texts and Coffin Texts, in which he is depicted in a fierce aspect, but he does not rise to prominence until the New Kingdom, when he is described as the "Greatest God of the Great Gods". Most of the construction of the temple complex at Karnak was centered on Khonsu during the Ramesside period.

claims.statement: A Karnak account makes him the great serpent fertilizing the cosmic egg.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kisah Karnak menjadikannya ular besar yang membuahi telur kosmis.
claims.quote: Khonsu is described as the great snake who fertilizes the Cosmic Egg in the creation of the world.

claims.statement: The Bentresh stela recounts healing a princess of Bekhten when Khonsu’s image arrives.
claims.statement_id: Stela Bentresh mengisahkan penyembuhan putri Bekhten setelah gambar Khonsu tiba.
claims.quote: Khonsu's reputation as a healer spread outside Egypt; the Bentresh stela records how a princess of Bekhten was instantly cured of an illness upon the arrival of an image of Khonsu. King Ptolemy IV, after he was cured of an illness, called himself "Beloved of Khonsu Who Protects His Majesty and Drives Away Evil Spirits".

claims.statement: His cult locations include Memphis, Hibis and Edfu.
claims.statement_id: Pusat kultusnya mencakup Memphis, Hibis, dan Edfu.
claims.quote: Locations of Khonsu's cult were Memphis, Hibis, and Edfu.

claims.statement: He is invoked for protection from wild animals and for healing.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipanggil untuk melindungi dari hewan liar dan membantu penyembuhan.
claims.quote: Khonsu was invoked to protect against wild animals, and aid with healing.

claims.statement: In the New Kingdom he is described as highly popular and greatest after Amun.
claims.statement_id: Pada Kerajaan Baru ia disebut sangat populer dan terbesar sesudah Amun.
claims.quote: By the time of the New Kingdom (1570-1069 BCE) he was extremely popular and worshipped as the greatest among the gods after Amun.

claims.statement: Neith is an Egyptian goddess associated with warfare and motherhood.
claims.statement_id: Neith adalah dewi Mesir yang berhubungan dengan peperangan dan keibuan.
claims.quote: was an ancient Egyptian goddess, possibly of Libyan origin. She was associated with warfare

claims.statement: Her martial emblem consists of crossed bows.
claims.statement_id: Lambang perangnya berupa busur bersilangan.
claims.quote: symbolized by her emblem of crossed bows

claims.statement: Texts describe her as the mother of Ra and Sobek.
claims.statement_id: Teks menyebutnya ibu Ra dan Sobek.
claims.quote: texts refer to her as the mother of deities such as the sun god Ra and the crocodile god Sobek.

claims.statement: In some myths she becomes creator of the world and Great Mother.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sejumlah mitos ia menjadi pencipta dunia dan Ibu Agung.
claims.quote: As a mother goddess, she was sometimes described as the creator of the world in Egyptian creation myths and referred to as the "Great Mother". She also played a role in funerary religion. Over time she became one of the four goddesses who protected the coffin and the internal organs of the deceased.

claims.statement: She belongs to the four goddesses protecting coffins and the deceased’s internal organs.
claims.statement_id: Ia termasuk empat dewi pelindung peti mati dan organ orang wafat.
claims.quote: she became one of the four goddesses who protected the coffin and the internal organs of the deceased.

claims.statement: Her main cult centre is Sais in the Nile Delta.
claims.statement_id: Pusat utama kultusnya adalah Sais di Delta Nil.
claims.quote: Her main cult center was the city of Sais in the western Nile Delta.

claims.statement: Greek writers identify her with Athena.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yunani mengidentifikasinya dengan Athena.
claims.quote: Greek writers identified her with the goddess Athena.

claims.statement: She is shown with Lower Egypt’s Red Crown and bow and arrows.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan memakai Mahkota Merah Mesir Hilir dan memegang busur serta anak panah.
claims.quote: Neith is typically depicted as a woman wearing the Red Crown of Lower Egypt and holding a bow and arrows. She is therefore often interpreted as a goddess of war and hunting. Her hieroglyphic symbol consists of two bows crossed over a shield.

claims.statement: She often carries a was-sceptre and an ankh.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering membawa tongkat was dan ankh.
claims.quote: As a deity, Neith is frequently shown carrying the was-sceptre (a symbol of power) and the ankh (a symbol of life). She was sometimes associated with Mehet-Weret, a cosmic cow goddess who gave birth to the sun daily.

claims.statement: The Opener of the Ways epithet may relate to warfare and guiding souls.
claims.statement_id: Gelar Pembuka Jalan dapat berhubungan dengan perang maupun penuntunan jiwa.
claims.quote: Neith possessed many roles in Egyptian religion. In early texts she was described as an “Opener of the Ways”, an epithet also used for the god Wepwawet. This title may refer to both her role in warfare and her function as a guide of souls in the afterlife.

claims.statement: The Mistress of the Bow epithet emphasizes her link with weapons.
claims.statement_id: Gelar Nyonya Busur menegaskan hubungannya dengan senjata.
claims.quote: one of her epithets was "Mistress of the Bow".

claims.statement: She mediates Horus and Set’s dispute over ruling Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Ia menengahi sengketa Horus dan Set mengenai pemerintahan Mesir.
claims.quote: the goddess who settles the question of whether Horus or Set should rule Egypt when the tribunal of the gods cannot decide.

claims.statement: Her statue occurs with Isis, Nephthys and Serket in Tutankhamun’s tomb.
claims.statement_id: Patungnya muncul bersama Isis, Nephthys, dan Serket dalam makam Tutankhamun.
claims.quote: Her statue appears with those of Isis, Nephthys, and Serket in Tutankhamun's tomb.

claims.statement: She guards Duamutef, a son of Horus protecting canopic jars.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjaga Duamutef, salah satu putra Horus pelindung bejana kanopik.
claims.quote: She is the guardian goddess over Duamutef, one of the Four Sons of Horus who watch over the canopic jars in the tombs

claims.statement: Mackenzie records recognition of Neith in the tradition concerning Mena.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mencatat pengakuan terhadap Neith dalam tradisi tentang Mena.
claims.quote: Mena also gave diplomatic recognition to Neith, the earth goddess of the Libyans

claims.statement: Anuket is an Egyptian goddess of the Nile cataracts and Lower Nubia.
claims.statement_id: Anuket adalah dewi Mesir bagi katarak Nil dan Nubia Hilir.
claims.quote: Anuket was the ancient Egyptian goddess of the cataracts of the Nile and Lower Nubia in general, worshipped especially at Elephantine near the First Cataract.

claims.statement: She is especially worshipped at Elephantine near the First Cataract.
claims.statement_id: Ia terutama dipuja di Elephantine dekat katarak pertama.
claims.quote: worshipped especially at Elephantine near the First Cataract.

claims.statement: Her name means Clasper or Embracer.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti pemeluk atau perengkuh.
claims.quote: Her name meant the "Clasper" or "Embracer".

claims.statement: In Greek interpretation she is equated with Hestia or Vesta.
claims.statement_id: Dalam interpretasi Yunani ia disetarakan dengan Hestia atau Vesta.
claims.quote: In the interpretatio graeca, she was considered equivalent to Hestia or Vesta.

claims.statement: One early association makes her a daughter of Ra.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu hubungan awal menempatkannya sebagai putri Ra.
claims.quote: She was originally the daughter of Ra, but was always related to Satet in some way. For example, both goddesses were called the "Eye of Ra", along with Bastet, Hathor, and Sekhmet. Also, they were both related in some way to the Uraeus.

claims.statement: She protects Egypt’s southern border and is connected with the Nile flood.
claims.statement_id: Ia melindungi perbatasan selatan Mesir dan berhubungan dengan banjir Nil.
claims.quote: Anuket was the goddess of the Nile flood and a protective goddess of the southern border of Egypt. Her posing with her arms outstretched may have been a visual reference to the shape of the Nile, with its two tributaries, and influenced her being called "the Embracer".

claims.statement: Her association with swift water also connects her with papyrus.
claims.statement_id: Hubungannya dengan arus cepat turut menghubungkannya dengan papirus.
claims.quote: She was associated with swift moving water, and this was the reason for her association with papyruses.

claims.statement: She forms a triad with Khnum and Satis.
claims.statement_id: Ia membentuk triad bersama Khnum dan Satis.
claims.quote: Anuket was part of a triad with the god Khnum, and the goddess Satis. She may have been the sister of the goddess Satis or she may have been a junior consort to Khnum instead.

claims.statement: Her temple is built on Seheil Island.
claims.statement_id: Kuilnya dibangun di Pulau Seheil.
claims.quote: A temple dedicated to Anuket was erected on the Island of Seheil. Inscriptions show that a shrine or altar was dedicated to her at this site by the 13th Dynasty pharaoh Sobekhotep III. Much later, during the 18th Dynasty, Amenhotep II dedicated a chapel to the goddess.

claims.statement: The Elephantine cult includes a river procession at the start of Shemu.
claims.statement_id: Kultus Elephantine mencakup prosesi sungai pada awal Shemu.
claims.quote: During the New Kingdom, Anuket's cult at Elephantine included a river procession of the goddess during the first month of Shemu. Inscriptions mention the processional festival of Khnum and Anuket during this period.

claims.statement: The accompanying historical source connects Anuket with fertility and the Aswan cataract.
claims.statement_id: Sumber sejarah pendamping menghubungkan Anuket dengan kesuburan dan katarak Aswan.
claims.quote: Anqet (Anukit or Anuket) - Goddess of fertility and the cataract of the Nile River at Aswan.

claims.statement: Budge’s translation places Anqet in the list of gods of Khnum’s Divine House.

claims.quote: a list of the names of the gods who dwell in the Divine House of Khnemu. The goddess of the star Sept (Sothis), the goddess Anqet

claims.statement_id: Khnum adalah dewa Mesir Hulu yang awalnya terkait katarak Nil.
claims.quote: was one of the earliest-known Egyptian deities in Upper Egypt, originally associated with the Nile cataract.

claims.statement: He regulates the annual Nile inundation.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengatur banjir Nil tahunan.
claims.quote: He held the responsibility of regulating the annual inundation of the river

claims.statement: He is regarded as creator of human bodies and the ka.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap pencipta tubuh manusia dan ka.
claims.quote: he eventually became known as the creator of human bodies and the life force kꜣ ("ka").

claims.statement: He shapes humans from clay on a potter’s wheel and places them in wombs.
claims.statement_id: Ia membentuk manusia dari tanah liat dengan roda tembikar, lalu menempatkannya dalam rahim.
claims.quote: Using a potter's wheel and clay, he fashioned these entities and placed them within their mothers' wombs.

claims.statement: He is also revered as creator of animals.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dihormati sebagai pencipta hewan.
claims.quote: was revered as the creator of the animal kingdom.

claims.statement: His worship continues from the First Dynasty to the Greco-Roman period.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaannya berlanjut dari Dinasti Pertama sampai masa Yunani-Romawi.
claims.quote: Worship of Khnum spanned from the First Dynasty and persisted even into the Greco-Roman period when rule by native dynasties had ended. Initially, his primary cult center was at Herwer in Middle Egypt.

claims.statement: He forms the Elephantine triad with Satis and Anuket.
claims.statement_id: Ia membentuk triad Elephantine bersama Satis dan Anuket.
claims.quote: At Elephantine, Khnum formed a divine triad alongside the Nubian goddesses Satis and Anuket.

claims.statement: The ram horns in his representations are linked with fertility and rebirth.
claims.statement_id: Tanduk domba dalam penggambarannya terkait kesuburan dan kelahiran kembali.
claims.quote: Khnum's primary function in the inception of human beings was typically portrayed with the horns of a ram, one of the sacred animals worshiped in Ancient Egypt, representing aspects such as fertility, rebirth, regeneration, and resurrection.

claims.statement: He bears the titles Potter God and Lord of Life.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki gelar Dewa Perajin Tembikar dan Penguasa Kehidupan.
claims.quote: the "Creator god", "Potter god", "Lord of Life", "Lord of the Field", "Lord of Esna", "the good protector", and "Lord of the crocodiles".

claims.statement: Elephantine and Esna are two centres of his worship.
claims.statement_id: Elephantine dan Esna menjadi dua pusat pemujaannya.
claims.quote: The worship of Khnum centered on two principal riverside sites, Elephantine and Esna, which were regarded as sacred sites. At Elephantine, he was worshipped alongside Satis and Anuket, while at Esna, he was worshipped alongside Menhit, Nebtu, Neith and Heka. Banebdjedet was the equivalent god in Lower Egypt. Khnum has also been related to the deity Min.

claims.statement: Humans shaped by Khnum are raised so Ra’s light gives them life.
claims.statement_id: Manusia hasil bentukan Khnum diangkat agar cahaya Ra memberi kehidupan.
claims.quote: then held them high so the light of Ra could shine upon them and give them life.

claims.statement: He is patron of potters and ceramic workers.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi pelindung perajin tembikar dan keramik.
claims.quote: He is the patron god of potters and those who work in ceramics.

claims.statement: The Great Potter title emphasizes his creative role.
claims.statement_id: Gelar Perajin Tembikar Agung menegaskan peran penciptanya.
claims.quote: Also known as "The Great Potter", Khenmu was an early god of Upper Egypt

claims.statement: Khepri is a scarab-faced god representing the rising sun in Egyptian religion.
claims.statement_id: Khepri adalah dewa berwajah kumbang skarab yang mewakili matahari terbit dalam agama Mesir.
claims.quote: is a scarab-faced god in ancient Egyptian religion who represents the rising or morning sun.

claims.statement: He also represents creation and renewal of life.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga mewakili penciptaan dan pembaruan kehidupan.
claims.quote: By extension, he can also represent creation and the renewal of life.

claims.statement: His name appears in the Pyramid Texts and Amduat.
claims.statement_id: Namanya disebut dalam Teks Piramida dan Amduat.
claims.quote: The name "Khepri" appeared in the Pyramid texts and usually included the scarab hieroglyph as a determinative or ideogram as a potential means to make any allusions to the god clear. Khepri is also mentioned in the Amduat, as the god is intrinsically linked to cycle of the sun and Ra's nightly journey through the Duat, the Egyptian underworld.

claims.statement: His name derives from a word meaning develop or create.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari kata yang berarti berkembang atau mencipta.
claims.quote: Khepri (ḫprj) is derived from the Egyptian language verb ḫpr, meaning to "develop" or "create". Khepri (ḫprj) can also be spelled "Kheper", which is the Egyptian term used to denote the sun god, the scarab beetle, and the verbs "to come into existence" or "to be born".

claims.statement: Beetles emerging from dung balls inspire the association with creation from nothing.
claims.statement_id: Kemunculan kumbang dari bola kotoran mendorong kaitan dengan penciptaan dari ketiadaan.
claims.quote: This caused ancient Egyptians to believe that these insects were created from nothingness.

claims.statement: The sun’s daily rebirth is associated with the scarab.
claims.statement_id: Kelahiran matahari setiap hari dikaitkan dengan skarab.
claims.quote: They also believed that each day the sun was reborn or created from nothing, thus explaining the connection made between the Sun and the scarab.

claims.statement: In the Amduat’s twelfth hour Khepri steers the solar barque.
claims.statement_id: Pada jam kedua belas Amduat, Khepri mengemudikan bahtera matahari.
claims.quote: In hour twelve of the Amduat, a newly reborn Khepri helms the solar barque that pushes the sun, moving the morning sun across the early day sky. This mirrors the manner in which a scarab beetle pushes large balls of dung along the ground, highlighting the relationship made between Khepri and the insects.

claims.statement: Scarab-shaped jewellery is used as rings and amulets.
claims.statement_id: Perhiasan berbentuk skarab dipakai sebagai cincin dan jimat.
claims.quote: Scarab-shaped accessories were common in ancient Egypt, as rings or amulets meant to be attached to necklaces were often fashioned in the shape of these insects.

claims.statement: He is regarded as a manifestation of Ra rather than a separate cult focus.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap sebagai manifestasi Ra, bukan pusat kultus tersendiri.
claims.quote: There was no cult devoted to Khepri, as he was seen as a manifestation of the more prominent solar deity Ra.

claims.statement: Khepri represents morning, Ra midday and Atum evening.
claims.statement_id: Khepri mewakili pagi, Ra tengah hari, dan Atum senja.
claims.quote: Khepri represented the morning sun, Ra was the midday sun, and Atum represented the evening sun.

claims.statement: The accompanying encyclopedia identifies Khepri as Ra’s morning aspect.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia pendamping menyebut Khepri aspek pagi Ra.
claims.quote: Khepri - An aspect of Ra the sun god in his morning form, represented by the scarab beetle.
