claims.statement: Apis is a sacred bull worshipped in the Memphis region of Egyptian religion.
claims.statement_id: Apis adalah banteng suci yang dipuja di daerah Memphis dalam agama Mesir.
claims.quote: was a sacred bull or multiple sacred bulls worshiped in the Memphis region

claims.statement: He is known as Hathor’s son.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikenal sebagai putra Hathor.
claims.quote: identified as the son of Hathor, a primary deity in the pantheon of ancient Egypt.

claims.statement: He mediates between humans and gods, originally Ptah.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi perantara manusia dengan dewa, awalnya Ptah.
claims.quote: Apis also served as an intermediary between humans and other powerful deities (originally Ptah, later Osiris, then Atum).

claims.statement: Excavation of Saqqara’s Serapeum reveals tombs of over sixty animals.
claims.statement_id: Penggalian Serapeum Saqqara menemukan makam lebih dari enam puluh hewan.
claims.quote: Auguste Mariette's excavation of the Serapeum of Saqqara revealed the tombs of more than sixty animals

claims.statement: Worship of an Apis bull is known from the First Dynasty at Memphis.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan banteng Apis diketahui sejak Dinasti Pertama di Memphis.
claims.quote: Worship of an Apis bull, experienced by ancient Egyptians as holy, has been known since the First Dynasty in Memphis, while worship of the Apis as a proper god, at least according to Manetho's Aegyptiaca, seems to be a later adoption, purportedly started during the reign of king Kaiechos (possibly Nebra) of the Second Dynasty.

claims.statement: After death Apis becomes Osorapis or Osiris-Apis.
claims.statement_id: Setelah mati, Apis menjadi Osorapis atau Osiris-Apis.
claims.quote: after death, he became Osorapis, i.e. the Osiris Apis

claims.statement: The Apis cult belongs to three major bull cults with Mnevis and Buchis.
claims.statement_id: Kultus Apis termasuk tiga kultus banteng besar bersama Mnevis dan Buchis.
claims.quote: Apis was the most popular of three great bull cults of ancient Egypt, the others being the cults of Mnevis and Buchis. All are related to the worship of Hathor or Bat, similar primary goddesses separated by region until unification that eventually merged as Hathor. The worship of Apis was continued by the Greeks and after them by the Romans, and lasted until almost 400 CE.

claims.statement: The bull symbolizes the king’s courage, strength and fighting spirit.
claims.statement_id: Banteng melambangkan keberanian, kekuatan, dan daya juang raja.
claims.quote: This animal was chosen because it symbolized the courageous heart, great strength, and fighting spirit of the king. Apis came to be considered a manifestation of the king, as bulls were symbols of strength and fertility, qualities that are closely linked with kingship.

claims.statement: He is sometimes shown with the solar disk between his horns.
claims.statement_id: Ia kadang digambarkan dengan cakram matahari di antara tanduknya.
claims.quote: Occasionally, Apis was pictured with the sun-disk symbol of his mother, Hathor, between his horns, being one of few deities ever associated with her symbol. When the disk was depicted on his head with his horns below and the triangular marking on his forehead, an ankh was suggested. That symbol always was closely associated with Hathor.

claims.statement: The chosen bull is identified by special markings including a white forehead triangle.
claims.statement_id: Banteng terpilih dikenali melalui tanda khusus termasuk segitiga putih di dahi.
claims.quote: It was required to have a white triangular marking upon its forehead

claims.statement: The Apis cult is described as an important and long-lived cult in Egyptian history.
claims.statement_id: Kultus Apis disebut salah satu yang penting dan berumur panjang dalam sejarah Mesir.
claims.quote: The Apis Cult was one of the most important and long-lived in the history of Egyptian culture.

claims.statement: Plutarch, as quoted by Mackenzie, describes Apis as begotten through generative moonlight.
claims.statement_id: Plutarch, dalam kutipan Mackenzie, menyebut Apis lahir melalui cahaya generatif bulan.
claims.quote: It was begotten", Plutarch was informed, "by a ray of generative light flowing from the moon.

claims.statement: Apis’s movements are interpreted as prophecies at the temple.
claims.statement_id: Gerakan Apis ditafsirkan sebagai nubuat di kuil.
claims.quote: At the temple, Apis was used as an oracle, his movements being interpreted as prophecies.

claims.statement: Apis’s breath is believed to cure disease.
claims.statement_id: Napas Apis dipercaya menyembuhkan penyakit.
claims.quote: His breath was believed to cure disease and his presence to bless those around with strength.

claims.statement: On certain holidays he is paraded with jewellery and flowers.
claims.statement_id: Pada hari tertentu ia diarak dengan perhiasan dan bunga.
claims.quote: he was led through the streets of the city, bedecked with jewelry and flowers.

claims.statement: Bes is an Egyptian deity protecting households, mothers, children and childbirth.
claims.statement_id: Bes adalah dewa Mesir pelindung rumah tangga, ibu, anak, dan kelahiran.
claims.quote: is an ancient Egyptian deity ... worshipped as a protector of households and, in particular, of mothers, children, and childbirth.

claims.statement: Beset is his feminine counterpart.
claims.statement_id: Beset adalah pasangan femininnya.
claims.quote: together with his feminine counterpart Beset

claims.statement: His worship spreads to Syria and the Balearic Islands.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaannya menyebar ke Siria dan Kepulauan Balearik.
claims.quote: Worship of Bes spread as far north as the area of Syria and as far west as the Balearic Islands (Ibiza) in Spain, and later into the Roman and Achaemenid Empires.

claims.statement: He watches over children and fights evil spirits during childbirth.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjaga anak dan menghadapi roh jahat saat perempuan melahirkan.
claims.quote: Bes was a household protector, becoming responsible– throughout ancient Egyptian history– for such varied tasks as killing snakes, fighting off evil spirits, watching after children, and aiding women in labour by fighting off evil spirits, and thus present with Taweret at births.

claims.statement: Unlike most Egyptian gods, his image faces forward.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari kebanyakan dewa Mesir, gambarnya menghadap depan.
claims.quote: Images of the deity, quite different from those of the other gods, were kept in homes. Normally Egyptian gods were shown in profile, but instead Bes appeared in full face portrait, ithyphallic, and sometimes in a soldier's tunic, so as to appear ready to launch an attack on any approaching evil. He scared away demons from houses, so his statue was put up as a protector.

claims.statement: His statue is placed in homes for protection against demons.
claims.statement_id: Patungnya dipasang di rumah sebagai perlindungan terhadap setan.
claims.quote: He scared away demons from houses, so his statue was put up as a protector.

claims.statement: Bes also symbolizes music, dance and sexual pleasure.
claims.statement_id: Bes juga mewakili musik, tari, dan kenikmatan seksual.

claims.quote: is a deity in Ancient Egyptian religion, the feminine counterpart of the air god Shu.

claims.statement: Her mythological function is less clear than that of Shu, but Egyptologists have suggested she is connected with moisture, based on a Pyramid Texts passage in which she produces water and on parallelism with Shu's connection with dry air.
claims.statement_id: Fungsi mitologis Tefnut kurang jelas dibanding Shu, tetapi para Egiptolog mengusulkan bahwa ia berkaitan dengan kelembapan, berdasarkan satu bagian Pyramid Texts tempat ia menghasilkan air dan berdasarkan kesejajaran dengan kaitan Shu pada udara kering.
claims.quote: Her mythological function is less clear than that of Shu, but Egyptologists have suggested she is connected with moisture, based on a passage in the Pyramid Texts in which she produces water, and on parallelism with Shu's connection with dry air.

claims.statement: Tefnut was also one of the goddesses who could function as the fiery Eye of Ra.
claims.statement_id: Tefnut juga salah satu dewi yang dapat berfungsi sebagai Mata Ra yang berapi.
claims.quote: She was also one of the goddesses who could function as the fiery Eye of Ra.

claims.statement: The name Tefnut has no certain etymology but may be an onomatopoeia of the sound of spitting, as Atum spits her out in some versions of the creation myth; in addition, her name was written as a mouth spitting in late texts.
claims.statement_id: Nama Tefnut tidak memiliki etimologi yang pasti, tetapi mungkin tiruan bunyi meludah, karena dalam beberapa versi mitos penciptaan Atum meludahkannya; selain itu, dalam teks-teks akhir namanya ditulis sebagai mulut yang meludah.
claims.quote: The name Tefnut has no certain etymology but it may be an onomatopoeia of the sound of spitting, as Atum spits her out in some versions of the creation myth. Additionally, her name was written as a mouth spitting in late texts.

claims.statement: Tefnut's grandchildren were Osiris, Isis, Set, Nephthys and, in some versions, Horus the Elder.
claims.statement_id: Cucu-cucu Tefnut adalah Osiris, Isis, Set, Nephthys, dan, dalam sebagian versi, Horus yang Tua.
claims.quote: Tefnut's grandchildren were Osiris, Isis, Set, Nephthys, and, in some versions, Horus the Elder.

claims.statement: Pyramid Text 527 says that Atum was creative in that he sneezed in Heliopolis, and that brother and sister were born, that is Shu and Tefnut.
claims.statement_id: Pyramid Text 527 menyatakan bahwa Atum bersifat kreatif karena ia bersin di Heliopolis, lalu kakak-beradik itu lahir, yaitu Shu dan Tefnut.
claims.quote: Pyramid Text 527 says, "Atum was creative in that he proceeded to sneeze while in Heliopolis. And brother and sister were born - that is Shu and Tefnut."

claims.statement: The Coffin Texts contain references to Shu being sneezed out by Atum from his nose and Tefnut being spat out like saliva.
claims.statement_id: Teks Peti Mati memuat rujukan bahwa Shu dibersinkan oleh Atum dari hidungnya, dan Tefnut diludahkan seperti air liur.
claims.quote: The Coffin Texts contain references to Shu being sneezed out by Atum from his nose, and Tefnut being spat out like saliva.

claims.statement: Tefnut is a leonine deity and appears as a human with a lioness head when depicted as part of the Great Ennead of Heliopolis. The other frequent depiction is as a lioness, but she can also be depicted as fully human.
claims.statement_id: Tefnut adalah dewi berwujud singa: ia tampil sebagai manusia berkepala singa betina ketika digambarkan sebagai bagian dari Ennead Agung Heliopolis. Penggambaran lain yang sering adalah sebagai singa betina, tetapi ia juga dapat digambarkan sepenuhnya sebagai manusia.
claims.quote: Tefnut is a leonine deity, and appears as human with a lioness head when depicted as part of the Great Ennead of Heliopolis. The other frequent depiction is as a lioness, but Tefnut can also be depicted as fully human.

claims.statement: Tefnut even assumes the role of the mistress of the flame, adorned with a flame to represent protection against enemies.
claims.statement_id: Tefnut bahkan berperan sebagai nyonya api, dihiasi nyala api sebagai lambang perlindungan terhadap musuh.
claims.quote: She even assumes the role of the mistress of the flame, where she is adorned with a flame to represent protection against enemies.

claims.statement: Heliopolis and Leontopolis were the primary cult centres of Tefnut.
claims.statement_id: Heliopolis dan Leontopolis adalah pusat pemujaan utama Tefnut.
claims.quote: Heliopolis and Leontopolis (now ell el-Muqdam) were the primary cult centres.

claims.statement: Tefnut was worshiped with Shu as a pair of lions in Leontopolis in the Nile Delta.
claims.statement_id: Tefnut dipuja bersama Shu sebagai sepasang singa di Leontopolis, di Delta Nil.
claims.quote: She was worshiped with Shu as a pair of lions in Leontopolis in the Nile Delta.

claims.statement: At Karnak, Tefnut formed part of the Ennead and was invoked in prayers for the health and wellbeing of the pharaoh.
claims.statement_id: Di Karnak, Tefnut menjadi bagian dari Ennead dan diseru dalam doa untuk kesehatan dan kesejahteraan firaun.
claims.quote: At Karnak, Tefnut formed part of the Ennead and was invoked in prayers for the health and wellbeing of the pharaoh.

claims.statement: As a lioness Tefnut could display a wrathful aspect and is said to have escaped to Nubia in a rage, jealous of her grandchildren's higher worship; she returned only after receiving the title "honorable" from Thoth.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai singa betina, Tefnut dapat menunjukkan sisi murka dan dikatakan melarikan diri ke Nubia dalam kemarahan karena cemburu pada pemujaan yang lebih tinggi bagi cucu-cucunya; ia baru kembali setelah menerima gelar "terhormat" dari Thoth.
claims.quote: As a lioness she could display a wrathful aspect and is said to have escaped to Nubia in a rage, jealous of her grandchildren's higher worship. Only after receiving the title "honorable" from Thoth, did she return.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Tefnut is the mother of Geb (earth) and Nut (sky), who were born so human beings could have somewhere to live.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Tefnut adalah ibu Geb (bumi) dan Nut (langit), yang lahir agar manusia punya tempat tinggal.
claims.quote: Tefnut is the mother of Geb (earth) and Nut (sky) who were born so human beings could have somewhere to live.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Shu, the god of the air, was born of Atum (Ra) at the beginning of creation and sent to create the world with his sister Tefnut, goddess of moisture. The two were gone so long that Atum came to miss them and sent his eye (the Eye of Ra) to find them; when the eye returned with them Atum was so happy he cried, and his tears created human beings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Shu, dewa udara, dilahirkan Atum (Ra) pada awal penciptaan dan diutus menciptakan dunia bersama saudarinya Tefnut, dewi kelembapan. Keduanya pergi begitu lama sampai Atum merindukan mereka dan mengirim matanya (Mata Ra) untuk mencari; ketika mata itu kembali bersama mereka, Atum begitu bahagia hingga menangis, dan air matanya menciptakan manusia.
claims.quote: Shu - The primordial god of the air whose name means "Emptiness". He was born at the beginning of creation of Atum (Ra) and sent to create the world with his sister Tefnut (goddess of moisture). The two were gone so long that Atum came to miss them and sent his eye (the Eye of Ra) in search of them. When the eye returned with them, Atum was so happy he cried and his tears created human beings.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Ruty, the twin lion gods who represented the eastern and western horizons, were originally associated with Shu and Tefnut as sky deities and eventually became linked with Ra and the solar barge.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Ruty, dewa kembar berwujud singa yang mewakili cakrawala timur dan barat, pada mulanya dikaitkan dengan Shu dan Tefnut sebagai dewa langit, lalu akhirnya dikaitkan dengan Ra dan perahu matahari.
claims.quote: Ruty - The twin lion gods who represented the eastern and western horizons. The name means "Pair of Lions". They were originally associated with Shu and Tefnut as sky deities and eventually became linked with Ra and the solar barge.

claims.statement: Budge writes that Tefnut was the twin sister of Shu and, as a power of nature, typified moisture or some aspect of the sun's heat.
claims.statement_id: Budge menulis bahwa Tefnut adalah saudari kembar Shu dan sebagai kekuatan alam ia melambangkan kelembapan atau salah satu aspek panas matahari.
claims.quote: TEFNUT was the twin-sister of Shu; as a power of nature she typified moisture or some aspect of the sun's heat

claims.statement: In a Book of the Dead chapter, the speaker declares that he knows the Souls of Annu, namely Ra, Shu and Tefnut.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah pasal Kitab Orang Mati, sang penutur menyatakan bahwa ia mengenal Jiwa-jiwa Annu, yaitu Ra, Shu, dan Tefnut.
claims.quote: I know the Souls of Annu, namely, Rā, Shu, and Tefnut.

claims.statement: In the creation legend translated by Budge, the god who speaks says that he was then alone, for he had not yet emitted Shu from himself nor spit out Tefnut, and no other existed who could work with him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda penciptaan terjemahan Budge, dewa yang berbicara mengatakan bahwa pada waktu itu ia sendirian karena belum mengeluarkan Shu dari dirinya dan belum meludahkan Tefnut, dan tidak ada yang lain yang dapat bekerja bersamanya.
claims.quote: I was [then] one by myself, for I had not emitted from myself the god Shu, and I had not spit out from myself the goddess Tefnut; and there existed no other who could work with me.

claims.statement: In a spell translated by Budge, the person addressed is told that his right eye is like Shu and his left eye like Tefnut, who are the children of Ra.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah mantra terjemahan Budge, yang dituju diberi tahu bahwa mata kanannya seperti Shu dan mata kirinya seperti Tefnut, yang adalah anak-anak Ra.
claims.quote: Thy right eye is like Shu, and thy left eye like Tefnut, who are the children of Ra.

claims.statement: Budge writes that Temu transferred the magical power of his life to Shu and Tefnut by embracing them.
claims.statement_id: Budge menulis bahwa Temu memindahkan daya magis hidupnya kepada Shu dan Tefnut dengan memeluk mereka.
claims.quote: Thus Temu transferred the magical power of his life to Shu and Tefnut by embracing them

claims.statement: During the 18th and 19th Dynasties, particularly during the Amarna Period, Tefnut was depicted in human form wearing a low flat headdress topped with sprouting plants.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa Dinasti ke-18 dan ke-19, terutama pada Periode Amarna, Tefnut digambarkan berwujud manusia dengan penutup kepala datar rendah yang dihiasi tanaman bertunas.
claims.quote: During the 18th and 19th Dynasties, particularly during the Amarna Period, Tefnut was depicted in human form wearing a low flat headdress, topped with sprouting plants.

claims.statement: The eye's violent aspect defends Ra against the agents of disorder that threaten his rule.
claims.statement_id: Sisi buas Mata Ra membela Ra dari para pelaku kekacauan yang mengancam kekuasaannya.
claims.quote: The eye's violent aspect defends Ra against the agents of disorder that threaten his rule.

claims.statement: The disastrous fury and rampages of the eye goddess, and the gods' efforts to appease her, are a prominent motif in Egyptian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Kemurkaan dan amukan dewi Mata yang membawa bencana, serta upaya para dewa menenangkannya, adalah motif menonjol dalam mitologi Mesir.
claims.quote: The disastrous fury and rampages of the eye goddess and the efforts of the gods to appease her are a prominent motif in Egyptian mythology.

claims.statement: In the Distant Goddess myth, with the solar eye gone Ra is vulnerable to his enemies and loses a large part of his power; the eye's absence and Ra's weakened state may refer to solar eclipses.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos Dewi Jauh, ketika Mata matahari pergi, Ra menjadi rentan terhadap musuh-musuhnya dan kehilangan sebagian besar kekuatannya; ketiadaan Mata itu dan melemahnya Ra mungkin merujuk pada gerhana matahari.
claims.quote: With the solar eye gone, Ra is vulnerable to his enemies and bereft of a large part of his power. The eye's absence and Ra's weakened state may be a mythological reference to solar eclipses.

claims.statement: Meanwhile the eye wanders in a distant land (Nubia, Libya or Punt) in the form of a wild feline, as dangerous and uncontrolled as the forces of chaos she is meant to subdue.
claims.statement_id: Sementara itu Mata mengembara di negeri jauh, yaitu Nubia, Libya, atau Punt, dalam wujud kucing liar yang berbahaya dan tak terkendali seperti kekuatan kekacauan yang seharusnya ia taklukkan.
claims.quote: Meanwhile, the eye wanders in a distant land—Nubia, Libya, or Punt. She takes the form of a wild feline, as dangerous and uncontrolled as the forces of chaos that she is meant to subdue.

claims.statement: In some accounts it is Shu who searches for Tefnut, who in this case represents the eye rather than an independent deity.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa kisah, Shu-lah yang mencari Tefnut, yang dalam hal ini mewakili Mata, bukan dewi yang berdiri sendiri.
claims.quote: In other accounts, it is Shu who searches for Tefnut, who in this case represents the eye rather than an independent deity.

claims.statement: When the goddess is at last placated, the retrieving god escorts her back to Egypt; her return marks the beginning of the inundation and the new year.
claims.statement_id: Ketika sang dewi akhirnya tenang, dewa yang menjemputnya mengantarnya kembali ke Mesir; kepulangannya menandai awal banjir tahunan dan tahun baru.
claims.quote: When the goddess is at last placated, the retrieving god escorts her back to Egypt. Her return marks the beginning of the inundation and the new year.

claims.statement: Tefnut and Shu once argued and Tefnut left Egypt for Nubia; Shu soon missed her, but she changed into a cat that destroyed any man or god that approached, until Thoth, disguised, eventually convinced her to return.
claims.statement_id: Tefnut dan Shu pernah bertengkar dan Tefnut meninggalkan Mesir menuju Nubia; Shu segera merindukannya, tetapi ia berubah menjadi kucing yang membinasakan setiap manusia atau dewa yang mendekat, sampai Thoth yang menyamar akhirnya berhasil membujuknya pulang.
claims.quote: Tefnut and Shu once argued, and Tefnut left Egypt for Nubia (which was always more temperate). It was said that Shu quickly decided that he missed her, but she changed into a cat that destroyed any man or god that approached. Thoth, disguised, eventually succeeded in convincing her to return.

claims.statement: In the earlier Pyramid Texts she is said to produce pure waters.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Teks Piramida yang lebih awal, ia dikatakan menghasilkan air yang murni dari tubuhnya.
claims.quote: In the earlier Pyramid Texts she is said to produce pure waters from her vagina.

claims.statement: At Heliopolis, Tefnut was one of the members of that city's great Ennead and is mentioned in connection with the purification of the wabet priest in the temple rite.
claims.statement_id: Di Heliopolis, Tefnut adalah salah satu anggota Ennead agung kota itu, dan disebut dalam kaitan dengan penyucian imam wabet sebagai bagian dari ritus kuil.
claims.quote: At Heliopolis, Tefnut was one of the members of that city's great Ennead, and is referred to in relation to the purification of the wabet (priest) as part of the temple rite.

claims.statement: According to Budge, originally these gods personified air and dryness and liquids respectively; with their creation the materials for building the atmosphere and sky came into being.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Budge, pada mulanya Shu dan Tefnut adalah perwujudan udara dan kekeringan serta cairan; dengan penciptaan mereka, bahan untuk membangun atmosfer dan langit pun muncul.
claims.quote: Originally these gods were the personifications of air and dryness, and liquids respectively; thus with their creation the materials for the construction of the atmosphere and sky came into being.

claims.statement: In the creation legend translated by Budge, Shu and Tefnut rejoiced and brought the creator his Eye (the Sun); afterwards he wept, and men and women sprang into being from the tears that came from his Eye.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda penciptaan yang diterjemahkan Budge, Shu dan Tefnut bergembira dan membawakan kepada sang pencipta Matanya (yaitu Matahari); setelah itu ia menangisinya, dan laki-laki serta perempuan muncul dari air mata yang keluar dari Matanya.
claims.quote: Then Shu and Tefnut rejoiced ... and they brought to me my Eye (i.e., the Sun). Now after these things I gathered together my members, and I wept over them, and men and women sprang into being from the tears which came forth from my Eye.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Atum (Ra) sent his children Shu and Tefnut out to create the world; when they returned he shed tears of joy that became human beings, who had nowhere to live, so Shu and Tefnut gave birth to Geb (earth) and Nut (sky).
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Atum (Ra) mengutus anak-anaknya Shu dan Tefnut untuk menciptakan dunia; saat mereka kembali, ia menangis bahagia dan air matanya menjadi manusia, yang belum punya tempat tinggal, sehingga Shu dan Tefnut melahirkan Geb (bumi) dan Nut (langit).
claims.quote: Atum (Ra) sent his children Shu and Tefnut out to create the world. When they returned, he was so happy he shed tears of joy which became human beings. These creatures had nowhere to live and so Shu and Tefnut mated to give birth to Geb (earth) and Nut (sky).

claims.statement: Ammit is an Egyptian being of the judgment of the dead, combining lion, hippopotamus and crocodile features.
claims.statement_id: Ammit adalah makhluk Mesir dalam pengadilan orang mati, berwujud gabungan singa, kuda nil, dan buaya.
claims.quote: was an ancient Egyptian goddess with the forequarters of a lion, the hindquarters of a hippopotamus, and the head of a crocodile

claims.statement: Her name means devourer or swallower of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti pelahap atau penelan orang mati.
claims.quote: means "devourer of the dead" ("devoureress of the dead") or "swallower of the dead"

claims.statement: The combination of three deadly Nile animals suggests that no one escapes annihilation even in the afterlife.
claims.statement_id: Gabungan tiga hewan berbahaya Nil menyiratkan pemusnahan yang tidak dapat dihindari, bahkan di akhirat.
claims.quote: The combination of three deadly animals of the Nile suggests that no one can escape annihilation, even in the afterlife.

claims.statement: She begins appearing in versions of the Book of the Dead in the New Kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Ia mulai muncul dalam versi Kitab Orang Mati pada Kerajaan Baru.
claims.quote: Versions of the Book of the Dead from the New Kingdom started to include Ammit. During the eighteenth dynasty, the crocodile-lion-hippopotamus hybrid was the conventional depiction of Ammit. She appeared in scenes showing the Judgment of the Dead, in tombs and funerary papyri.

claims.statement: Ammit is feared rather than a focus of worship.
claims.statement_id: Ammit ditakuti alih-alih menjadi pusat pemujaan.
claims.quote: Unlike other gods featured in ancient Egyptian religion, Ammit was not worshipped. Instead, Ammit was feared and believed to be a demon rather than a deity, due to her role as the 'devourer of the dead'. During the New Kingdom, deities and demons were differentiated by having a cult or center of worship.

claims.statement: Ammit devours hearts of souls not justified by Osiris.
claims.statement_id: Ammit menelan hati jiwa yang gagal memperoleh pembenaran Osiris.
claims.quote: devoured the hearts of those souls which were not justified by Osiris.

claims.statement: Serket is an Egyptian goddess protecting against scorpion stings and bites.
claims.statement_id: Serket adalah dewi Mesir pelindung terhadap sengatan dan gigitan kalajengking.
claims.quote: is the goddess of protection against the venomous stings and bites of scorpions in Egyptian mythology.

claims.statement: She is shown with a scorpion on her head, an ankh and a was-sceptre.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan dengan kalajengking di kepala, ankh, dan tongkat was.
claims.quote: Serket is often depicted as a woman whose head is surmounted by a scorpion ... an ankh in one hand, and a was-sceptre in her other.

claims.statement: She is associated with healing, magic and protection.
claims.statement_id: Ia berhubungan dengan penyembuhan, sihir, dan perlindungan.
claims.quote: She is associated with healing, magic, and protection. Another interpretation of her name is, 'she who gives breath.' As many of the venomous creatures of Egypt could prove fatal, Serket was considered a protector of the dead, particularly being associated with venoms and fluids that cause stiffening.

claims.statement: She protects embalming tents and Qebehsenuef, a guardian of canopic jars.
claims.statement_id: Ia melindungi tempat pembalseman dan Qebehsenuef penjaga bejana kanopik.
claims.quote: During the Old Kingdom she held a protective role around the throne of the king. However, her primary role was with the funerary cult. She was said to be the protector of the tents of embalmers and is one of the tutelary goddesses depicted on the canopic chest which contains four canopic jars.

claims.statement: The Book of Two Ways makes her guardian of a bend in the underworld path.
claims.statement_id: Kitab Dua Jalan menempatkannya sebagai penjaga belokan jalan dunia bawah.
claims.quote: During the Middle Kingdom, Egyptian myth says that Serket's help is required in the Underworld where according to the Book of the Two Ways she guards a twist in the pathway. She is also given credit for binding and containing the snake deity, Apophis (or Apep).

claims.statement: A golden statue of Serket is found in Tutankhamun’s tomb.
claims.statement_id: Patung emas Serket ditemukan dalam makam Tutankhamun.
claims.quote: She is best known from her golden statue found in the tomb of Tutankhamun.

claims.statement: Taweret is an Egyptian goddess protecting childbirth and fertility.
claims.statement_id: Taweret adalah dewi Mesir pelindung kelahiran dan kesuburan.
claims.quote: is the protective goddess of childbirth and fertility.

claims.statement: Her name means the Great One.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti Yang Agung.
claims.quote: The name "Taweret" means "she who is great" or simply "great one"

claims.statement: She takes the form of a bipedal female hippopotamus with lion and crocodile features.
claims.statement_id: Ia berupa kuda nil betina berkaki dua dengan unsur singa dan buaya.
claims.quote: The deity is typically depicted as a bipedal female hippopotamus with feline attributes, pendulous female human breasts, the limbs and paws of a lion, and the back and tail of a Nile crocodile.

claims.statement: She is closely associated with the hippopotamus goddesses Ipet, Reret and Hedjet.
claims.statement_id: Ia dekat dengan dewi kuda nil Ipet, Reret, dan Hedjet.
claims.quote: From her ideological conception, Taweret was closely grouped with (and is often indistinguishable from) several other protective hippopotamus goddesses: Ipet, Reret, and Hedjet. Some scholars even interpret these goddesses as aspects of the same deity, considering their universally shared role as protective household goddesses.

claims.statement: Her image adorns magical knives or wands used in infant-protection rites.
claims.statement_id: Gambarnya menghiasi pisau atau tongkat magis untuk ritual perlindungan bayi.
claims.quote: It was not until the Middle Kingdom of Egypt (c. 2055–1650 BCE) that Taweret became featured more prominently as a figure of religious devotion. Her image adorns magical objects, the most notable of which being a common type of "wand" or "knife" carved from hippopotamus ivory that was likely used in rituals associated with birth and the protection of infants.

claims.statement: Taweret is also called Bes’s consort in the accompanying source.
claims.statement_id: Taweret juga disebut pasangan Bes dalam sumber pendamping.
claims.quote: She is further identified as the consort of Bes, the dwarf god of childbirth, sexuality, humor, and war.

claims.statement: Nun personifies the primordial watery abyss in Egyptian religion, from which Ra arises.
claims.statement_id: Nun adalah personifikasi jurang air primordial dalam agama Mesir, tempat Ra muncul.
claims.quote: in ancient Egyptian religion, is the personification of the primordial watery abyss which existed at the time of creation and from which the creator sun god Ra arose.

claims.statement: He is an Ogdoad member representing chaos before creation.
claims.statement_id: Ia anggota Ogdoad yang mewakili kekacauan sebelum penciptaan.
claims.quote: Nun is one of the eight deities of the Ogdoad representing ancient Egyptian primordial Chaos from which the primordial mound arose. Nun can be seen as the first of all the gods and the creator of reality and personification of the cosmos. Nun is also considered the god that will destroy existence and return everything to the Nun whence it came. No cult was addressed to Nun.

claims.statement: He is also seen as returning existence to its primordial condition.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dipandang mengembalikan keberadaan ke keadaan primordial.
claims.quote: Nun is also considered the god that will destroy existence and return everything to the Nun whence it came.

claims.statement: Naunet is his consort or feminine aspect.
claims.statement_id: Naunet adalah pasangan atau aspek femininnya.
claims.quote: Nun's consort (or his female aspect) was the goddess Nunut or Naunet (Ancient Egyptian: 𓏌𓐱𓏌𓐰𓏌𓐰𓇯𓈗𓏏𓐰𓆇𓁐, romanized: nnwt).

claims.statement: The world’s first mound emerges from Nun’s waters.
claims.statement_id: Bukit pertama dunia muncul dari air Nun.
claims.quote: In ancient Egyptian creation accounts, the original mound of land comes forth from the waters of the Nun.

claims.statement: Budge calls Nu father of the gods and primordial watery source of all things.
claims.statement_id: Budge menyebut Nu sebagai ayah para dewa dan sumber air primordial semua hal.
claims.quote:
NU was the "father of the gods," and progenitor of the "great company
  of the gods"; he was the primeval watery mass out of which all things
  came.

claims.statement: Wadjet is an Egyptian goddess originally worshipped at Dep or Buto in Lower Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Wadjet adalah dewi Mesir yang semula dipuja di Dep atau Buto, Mesir Hilir.
claims.quote: was originally the ancient Egyptian local goddess of the city of Dep or Buto in Lower Egypt

claims.statement: She is connected with the Eye of Ra and Eye of Horus symbols.
claims.statement_id: Ia terkait lambang Mata Ra dan Mata Horus.
claims.quote: Wadjet was closely associated in ancient Egyptian religion with the Eye of Ra and the Eye of Horus symbols, each powerful protective deities. The hieroglyph for her eye is shown below; sometimes two are shown in the sky of religious images. There is little consensus on which eye is truly tied to Wadjet as both have some importance to her.

claims.statement: Her name derives from the term for papyrus as a symbol of Lower Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari istilah papirus sebagai lambang Mesir Hilir.
claims.quote: The name Wadjet is derived from the term for the symbol of her domain, Lower Egypt, the papyrus. Its hieroglyphs differ from those of the Green Crown or Deshret of Lower Egypt only by the determinative, which in the case of the crown was a picture of the Green Crown and, in the case of the goddess, a rearing cobra.

claims.statement: With Nekhbet she becomes a protector of all Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Bersama Nekhbet ia menjadi pelindung seluruh Mesir.
claims.quote: Wadjet was said to be the matron and protector of Lower Egypt in her cobra form, and upon unification with her sister Nekhbet, Goddess of Upper Egypt, the joint protector and patron of all of Egypt. Scenes of the two sisters together as two cobras can be found in King Sety I's tomb, located in the Valley of the Kings.

claims.statement: One myth makes her Horus’s nurse, helping Isis protect him.
claims.statement_id: Satu mitos menjadikannya pengasuh Horus yang membantu Isis melindunginya.
claims.quote: In another myth, Wadjet was said to be the nurse of the infant god Horus. With the help of his mother Isis, they protected Horus from his treacherous uncle, Set, when they took refuge in the swamps of the Nile Delta.

claims.statement: This source tells of Wadjet planting the first papyrus and helping Isis raise Horus.
claims.statement_id: Sumber ini mengisahkan Wadjet menanam papirus pertama dan membantu Isis membesarkan Horus.
claims.quote: She planted the first papyrus plants, laid out the papyrus fields in the swamps of the Nile Delta, and helped Isis raise Horus there

claims.statement: Nekhbet is an Egyptian goddess protecting Nekheb and later Upper Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Nekhbet adalah dewi Mesir pelindung Nekheb yang kemudian melindungi Mesir Hulu.
claims.quote: is an early predynastic local goddess in Egyptian mythology, who was the patron of the city of Nekheb

claims.statement: Her early shrine is at Nekheb or El Kab.
claims.statement_id: Kuil awalnya berada di Nekheb atau El Kab.
claims.quote: One of Egypt's earliest temples was the shrine of Nekhbet at Nekheb (also referred to as El Kab). It was the companion city to Nekhen, the religious and political capital of Upper Egypt, at the end of the Predynastic period (c. 3200–3100 BC) and probably, also during the Early Dynastic Period (c. 3100–2686 BC).

claims.statement: She and Wadjet appear as the Two Ladies in royal titles.
claims.statement_id: Ia dan Wadjet tampil sebagai Dua Nyonya dalam gelar kerajaan.
claims.quote: Nekhbet was the tutelary deity of Upper Egypt. Nekhbet and her Lower Egyptian counterpart Wadjet often appeared together as the "Two Ladies". One of the titles of each ruler was the Nebty name, which began with the hieroglyphs for [s/he] of the Two Ladies....

claims.statement: She is depicted as a vulture.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai burung nasar.
claims.quote: In art, Nekhbet was depicted as a vulture.

claims.statement: She hovers with spread wings and a shen symbol for eternal protection.
claims.statement_id: Ia melayang dengan sayap terentang dan simbol shen sebagai perlindungan kekal.
claims.quote: Nekhbet usually was depicted hovering, with her wings spread above the royal image, clutching a shen symbol (representing eternal encircling protection), frequently in her claws.

claims.statement: The accompanying source confirms Nekhbet and Wadjet as the Two Ladies.
claims.statement_id: Sumber pendamping menegaskan pasangan Nekhbet dan Wadjet sebagai Dua Nyonya.
claims.quote: Nekhbet - A protector goddess in the form of a vulture who guarded Upper Egypt. She was associated with Wadjet, protector of Lower Egypt. The two are referred to as "The Two Ladies".

claims.statement: The Great Ennead is a group of nine Egyptian gods worshipped at Heliopolis.
claims.statement_id: Ennead Agung adalah kelompok sembilan dewa Mesir yang dipuja di Heliopolis.
claims.quote: The Ennead or Great Ennead was a group of nine deities in Egyptian mythology worshipped at Heliopolis: the sun god Atum; his children Shu and Tefnut; their children Geb and Nut; and their children Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys. The Ennead sometimes includes Horus the Elder; an ancient form of the falcon god, not the son of Osiris and Isis.

claims.statement: Its members include Atum, Shu, Tefnut, Geb, Nut, Osiris, Isis, Set and Nephthys.
claims.statement_id: Anggotanya mencakup Atum, Shu, Tefnut, Geb, Nut, Osiris, Isis, Set, dan Nephthys.
claims.quote: the sun god Atum; his children Shu and Tefnut; their children Geb and Nut; and their children Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys.

claims.statement: Heliopolis’s Ennead is one of several groups of nine gods.
claims.statement_id: Ennead Heliopolis merupakan salah satu dari beberapa kelompok sembilan dewa.
claims.quote: The Great Ennead was only one of several such groupings of nine deities in ancient Egypt.

claims.statement: The word ennead comes through Latin from Greek meaning nine.
claims.statement_id: Kata ennead berasal melalui bahasa Latin dari bahasa Yunani yang berarti sembilan.
claims.quote: The English name ennead is a borrowing via Latin of the Greek name enneás (ἐννεάς), meaning "the nine". The term was a calque of the Egyptian name, written psḏt and also meaning "the Nine". Its original pronunciation is uncertain, since hieroglyphs do not record vowels, but may have been /piˈsiːcʼat/ in Old Egyptian, /piˈsiːtʼaʔ/ in Middle Egyptian, and /pəˈsiːtʼə/ in Late Egyptian.

claims.statement: The Pyramid Texts mention the Great, Lesser, Dual and Seven Enneads.
claims.statement_id: Teks Piramida menyebut Ennead Agung, Kecil, Ganda, dan Tujuh Ennead.
claims.quote: The Pyramid Texts of Dynasties V and VI mention the "Great Ennead", the "Lesser Ennead", the "Dual Ennead", and the "Seven Enneads".

claims.statement: The Ennead judges Set and Horus’s dispute over the throne.
claims.statement_id: Ennead mengadili sengketa Set dan Horus mengenai takhta.
claims.quote: These nine gods decide whether Set or Horus should rule in the story The Contendings of Horus and Set.

claims.statement: Monthu or Montu is an Egyptian falcon war god, especially worshipped in Upper Egypt and Thebes.
claims.statement_id: Monthu atau Montu adalah dewa perang elang Mesir, terutama dipuja di Mesir Hulu dan Thebes.
claims.quote: Montu was a falcon-war god in the ancient Egyptian religion, an embodiment of the conquering vitality of the pharaoh. He was particularly worshipped in Upper Egypt and in the district of Thebes.

claims.statement: His name is transcribed mntw and associated with the meaning nomad.
claims.statement_id: Namanya ditranskripsikan mntw dan dikaitkan dengan makna pengembara.
claims.quote: Montu's name, shown in Egyptian hieroglyphs to the right, is technically transcribed as mntw (meaning "Nomad"). Because of the difficulty in transcribing Egyptian vowels, it is often realized as Mont, Monthu, Montju, Ment or Menthu.

claims.statement: He is linked with Ra as Montu-Ra and confronts enemies of Maat.
claims.statement_id: Ia terkait Ra sebagai Montu-Ra dan menghadapi musuh Maat.
claims.quote: A very ancient god, Montu was originally a manifestation of the scorching effect of Ra, the sun – and as such often appeared under the epithet Montu-Ra. The destructiveness of this characteristic led to him gaining characteristics of a warrior, and eventually becoming a widely revered war-god.

claims.statement: The sacred bull Buchis becomes his manifestation.
claims.statement_id: Banteng suci Buchis menjadi manifestasinya.
claims.quote: Because of the association of raging bulls with strength and war, the Egyptians also believed that Montu manifested himself as a white, black-snouted bull named Buchis (hellenization of the original Bakha: a living bull revered in Armant) — to the point that, in the Late Period (7th-4th centuries BC), Montu was depicted with a bull's head too.

claims.statement: Art depicts him as falcon- or bull-headed with a solar disk and feathers.
claims.statement_id: Seni menggambarkannya berkepala elang atau banteng dengan cakram matahari dan bulu.
claims.quote: In Egyptian art, Montu was depicted as a falcon-headed or bull-headed man, with his head surmounted by the solar disk (because of his conceptual link with Ra) with either a double or singular uraeus, and two feathers. The falcon was a symbol of the sky and the bull was a symbol of strength and war.

claims.statement: The Greeks equate Montu with Apollo.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yunani menyetarakan Montu dengan Apollo.
claims.quote: The Greeks equated him with Apollo

claims.statement: Nefertem is an Egyptian god emerging as a lotus from primordial waters at creation.
claims.statement_id: Nefertem adalah dewa Mesir yang muncul sebagai teratai dari air primordial saat penciptaan.
claims.quote: was a lotus flower at the creation of the world, who had arisen from the primal waters.

claims.statement: He represents the first sunlight and the scent of the Egyptian blue lotus.
claims.statement_id: Ia mewakili sinar matahari pertama dan aroma teratai biru Mesir.
claims.quote: Nefertem represented both the first sunlight and the delightful smell of the Egyptian blue lotus flower

claims.statement: Ptah becomes his father, while Sekhmet or Bastet may be called his mother.
claims.statement_id: Ptah menjadi ayahnya, sedangkan Sekhmet atau Bastet dapat disebut ibunya.
claims.quote: Nefertem was eventually seen as the son of the creator god Ptah, and the goddesses Sekhmet and Bast were sometimes called his mother. In art, Nefertem is usually depicted as a beautiful young man having blue water-lily flowers around his head. As the son of Bastet, he also sometimes has the head of a lion or is a lion or cat reclining.

claims.statement: He is often a young man with blue lotus flowers around his head.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering berupa pemuda dengan bunga teratai biru di kepala.
claims.quote: Nefertem is usually depicted as a beautiful young man having blue water-lily flowers around his head.

claims.statement: A bust of Tutankhamun emerging from a lotus is a notable depiction of Nefertem.
claims.statement_id: Patung kepala Tutankhamun muncul dari teratai merupakan penggambaran terkenal Nefertem.
claims.quote: One of the most notable depictions of Nefertem is the Head of Nefertem, a wooden bust depicting a young king Tutankhamun as Nefertem with his head emerging from a lotus flower.

claims.statement: Nefertem is invoked for healing through aromas in Egyptian medicine.
claims.statement_id: Nefertem dipanggil untuk penyembuhan melalui aroma dalam pengobatan Mesir.
claims.quote: In Egyptian medicine he was called upon for healing aromas to cure disease and associated with incense.

claims.statement: Heqet is an Egyptian fertility goddess depicted as a frog.
claims.statement_id: Heqet adalah dewi kesuburan Mesir yang digambarkan sebagai katak.
claims.quote: Heqet (Egyptian ḥqt, also ḥqtyt "Heqtit"), sometimes spelled Heket, is an Egyptian goddess of fertility, identified with Hathor, represented in the form of a frog.

claims.statement: The frog is linked with the annual Nile flood and fertility.
claims.statement_id: Katak berkaitan dengan banjir tahunan Nil dan kesuburan.
claims.quote:
To the Egyptians, the frog was an ancient symbol of fertility, related to the annual flooding of the Nile. 
Heqet was originally the female counterpart of Khnum, or the wife of Khnum, and eventually she also became the mother of Heru-ur.
It has been proposed that her name is the origin of the name of Hecate, the Greek goddess of witchcraft.

claims.statement: Her cult is known from at least the Early Dynastic Period.
claims.statement_id: Kultusnya diketahui setidaknya sejak masa Dinasti Awal.
claims.quote: The beginning of her cult dates to the Early Dynastic Period at least. Her name was part of the names of some high-born Second Dynasty individuals buried at Helwan, such as prince Nisuheqet, and was mentioned on a stela of Wepemnofret and in the Pyramid Texts. Early frog statuettes are often thought to be depictions of her.

claims.statement: She is regarded as wife of Khnum, who shapes children’s bodies on a potter’s wheel.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap sebagai istri Khnum yang membentuk tubuh anak dengan roda tembikar.
claims.quote: Heqet was considered the wife of Khnum, who formed the bodies of new children on his potter's wheel.

claims.statement: In the Osiris myth she breathes life into Horus at birth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos Osiris ia memberikan napas hidup kepada Horus saat lahir.
claims.quote: In the Osiris myth, it was Heqet who breathed life into the new body of Horus at birth, as she was a goddess of the last moments of birth. As the birth of Horus became more intimately associated with the resurrection of Osiris, so Heqet's role became one more closely associated with resurrection.

claims.statement: The accompanying source depicts her as a frog or frog-headed woman.
claims.statement_id: Sumber pendamping menggambarkannya sebagai katak atau perempuan berkepala katak.
claims.quote: Heqet (Heket) - Goddess of fertility and childbirth, depicted as a frog or a woman with the head of a frog.

claims.statement: Seshat is the Egyptian goddess of writing, wisdom and knowledge.
claims.statement_id: Seshat adalah dewi penulisan, kebijaksanaan, dan pengetahuan Mesir.
claims.quote: was the ancient Egyptian goddess of writing, wisdom, and knowledge.

claims.statement: Seshat is the goddess of books, notations and measurements in the accompanying source.
claims.statement_id: Seshat adalah dewi buku, catatan, dan pengukuran dalam sumber pendamping.
claims.quote: She was the goddess of writing, books, notations, and measurements.

claims.statement: She is depicted helping Khasekhemwy in the stretching-the-cord ritual.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan membantu Khasekhemwy dalam ritual merentangkan tali.
claims.quote: she was shown conducting the "stretching the cord" ritual with Khasekhemwy.

claims.statement: The Pyramid Texts call her Lady of Builders.
claims.statement_id: Teks Piramida memanggilnya Nyonya Para Pembangun.
claims.quote: In the Pyramid Texts, she is identified as an aspect of Nephthys and is invoked as the 'Lady of Builders.'

claims.statement: Art shows a seven-pointed emblem above her head.
claims.statement_id: Seni memperlihatkan lambang berujung tujuh di atas kepalanya.
claims.quote: In ancient Egyptian art, she was depicted as a woman with a seven-pointed emblem above her head or extending from a headband. This emblem was the origin of an alternate name for Seshat, Sefkhet-Abwy, which may be translated as "seven-horned". She was frequently shown in a leopard-skin or dress, sometimes with a robe layered under a skin.

claims.statement: She is patron of public and private libraries.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi pelindung perpustakaan umum maupun pribadi.
claims.quote: She is the patroness of libraries, both public and private

claims.statement: Sokar is a falcon god of the Memphite necropolis in Egyptian religion.
claims.statement_id: Sokar adalah dewa elang kawasan pemakaman Memphis dalam agama Mesir.
claims.quote: is a hawk or falcon god of the Memphite necropolis in the Ancient Egyptian religion

claims.statement: His connection with Ptah and Osiris produces Ptah-Sokar-Osiris.
claims.statement_id: Hubungannya dengan Ptah dan Osiris menghasilkan Ptah-Sokar-Osiris.
claims.quote: Although the meaning of his name remains uncertain, the Egyptians in the Pyramid Texts linked his name to the anguished cry of Osiris to Isis 'Sy-k-ri' ('hurry to me'), or possibly skr, meaning "cleaning the mouth". In the underworld, Sokar is strongly linked with two other gods, Ptah the Creator god and chief god of Memphis, and Osiris the god of the dead.

claims.statement: He is often a mummified hawk or a hawk’s head emerging from a mound.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering berupa elang bermumi atau kepala elang yang muncul dari bukit.
claims.quote: Sokar was usually depicted as a mummified hawk and sometimes as a mound from which the head of a hawk appears. Here he is called 'he who is on his sand'. Sometimes, he is shown on his hennu barque which was an elaborate sledge for negotiating the sandy necropolis. One of his titles was 'He of Restau' which means the place of 'openings' or tomb entrances.

claims.statement: The Amduat shows him standing on a serpent between two wings.
claims.statement_id: Amduat menggambarkannya berdiri di atas ular di antara dua sayap.
claims.quote: In the New Kingdom Book of the Underworld, the Amduat, he is shown standing on the back of a serpent between two spread wings; as an expression of freedom this suggests a connection with resurrection or perhaps a satisfactory transit of the underworld.

claims.statement: The Book of the Dead says he fashions silver bowls.
claims.statement_id: Kitab Orang Mati menyebutnya membuat mangkuk perak.
claims.quote: Sokar, possibly through his association with Ptah, has a connection with artisans. In the Book of the Dead, he is said to fashion silver bowls and at Tanis a silver coffin of Sheshonq II has been discovered decorated with the iconography of Sokar.

claims.statement: The accompanying source places Sokar as guardian of the underworld entrance.
claims.statement_id: Sumber pendamping menempatkan Sokar sebagai penjaga pintu masuk dunia bawah.
claims.quote: guardian of the entrance to the underworld

claims.statement: Wepwawet is an Egyptian jackal deity of funerals, war and royalty, with a cult centre at Asyut.
claims.statement_id: Wepwawet adalah dewa jakal Mesir terkait pemakaman, perang, dan kerajaan, dengan pusat kultus di Asyut.
claims.quote: was originally a jackal deity of funerary rites, war, and royalty, whose cult centre was Asyut in Upper Egypt

claims.statement: His name means opener of the ways.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti pembuka jalan.
claims.quote: His name means opener of the ways and he is often depicted as a wolf standing at the prow of a solar-boat.

claims.statement: He opens ways through the Duat for spirits of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Ia membuka jalan melalui Duat bagi roh orang mati.
claims.quote: Over time, the connection to war and thus to death led to Wepwawet also being seen as one who opened the ways to, and through, Duat, for the spirits of the dead. Through this, Wepwawet became associated with Anubis, a deity that was worshiped in Asyut, eventually being considered his brother.

claims.statement: The Pyramid Texts place his birth in Wadjet’s sacred shrine.
claims.statement_id: Teks Piramida menempatkan kelahirannya di tempat suci Wadjet.
claims.quote: The Pyramid Texts state that Wepwawet was born in the Peru-nu, the sacred shrine of the goddess Wadjet, while an alternative myth suggests he emerged from a tamarisk bush. Consequently, Wepwawet is often confused with Anubis. This deity appears in the temple of Seti I at Abydos.

claims.statement: He may be depicted as a black jackal or jackal-headed man.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat digambarkan sebagai jakal hitam atau laki-laki berkepala jakal.
claims.quote: In Egyptian art, Wepwawet was depicted as a black jackal, or as a man with the head of a jackal. In the temple of Seti I at Abydos, Wepwawet appears to have grey-colored fur, though this is likely due to loss of pigmentation, as elsewhere in the temple, black paint is almost entirely faded. In rare cases, he appears in fully human form.

claims.statement: The accompanying source connects Wepwawet-Ra with the sun god Ra.
claims.statement_id: Sumber pendamping mengaitkan Wepwawet-Ra dengan dewa matahari Ra.
claims.quote: as Wepwawet-Ra, with the sun god Ra.

claims.statement: Anat is a goddess of warfare and hunting known from Ugaritic texts.
claims.statement_id: Anat adalah dewi perang dan perburuan yang dikenal dari teks Ugarit.
claims.quote: was a goddess associated with warfare and hunting, best known from the Ugaritic texts.

claims.statement: In the Baal Cycle she helps Baal obtain kingship and avenges his death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Siklus Baal ia membantu Baal memperoleh kekuasaan dan membalaskan kematiannya.
claims.quote: In Ugarit, Anat was one of the main goddesses, and regularly received offerings, as attested in texts written both in the local Ugaritic language and in Hurrian. She also frequently appears in myths, including the Baal Cycle and the Epic of Aqhat.

claims.statement: Anat enters Egypt in the Bronze Age and is prominent under Ramesses II.
claims.statement_id: Anat masuk ke Mesir pada Zaman Perunggu dan penting pada masa Ramses II.
claims.quote: At some point in time in the Bronze Age, either during the reign of Hyksos or shortly after its end, Anat was introduced to Egypt, and achieved a degree of prominence during the reign of Ramesses II, whose devotion to her is well attested. Evidence for Egyptian worship of Anat is also available from various sites in Palestine which were controlled by the pharaohs in the Bronze Age.

claims.statement: Early scholarship considers her a goddess of sexual fertility, but that is no longer scholarly consensus.
claims.statement_id: Kajian awal menganggapnya dewi kesuburan seksual, tetapi itu bukan lagi konsensus para ahli.
claims.quote: Anat was characterized as a fertility goddess associated with human sexuality in early scholarship, but despite the occasional modern support, this view is no longer the consensus among experts. Proposed etymologies of her name and interpretations of texts she appears in are a subject of criticism.

claims.statement: According to Lambert’s theory, she originates in Amorite tradition.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teori Lambert, ia berasal dari tradisi Amori.
claims.quote: In the light of Lambert's theory, Anat, like her presumed forerunner Ḫanat, would be an Amorite deity in origin.

claims.statement: One version of the Contendings of Horus and Set makes her Set’s consort at Neith’s suggestion.
claims.statement_id: Satu versi Contendings of Horus and Set menjadikannya pasangan Set atas saran Neith.
claims.quote: In one version of The Contendings of Horus and Set, she is given as a consort to Set at the suggestion of the goddess Neith.
